title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, and L.-M. Duan

Quantum networks and quantum repeaters represent the promising avenues for building large-scale quantum information systems, serving as foundational infrastructure for distributed quantum computing, long-distance quantum communication, and networked quantum sensing. A critical step in realizing a fu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber, a key step toward quantum repeaters.
motivation: Building large-scale quantum networks requires long-distance entanglement distribution; ion traps are promising but face challenges in connecting remote nodes.
method: Trapped ions generate entangled photon pairs via cavity QED; one photon is stored in a temporal multimode quantum memory while the other is transmitted through 1.2 km fiber; entanglement is verified via Bell inequality violation.
result: Achieved ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km with high fidelity, demonstrating temporal multiplexing and memory-enhanced quantum networking.
conclusion: This work validates a practical architecture for quantum repeaters using trapped ions and temporal multiplexing, advancing scalable quantum networks.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature Gibbs states of fermionic systems are convex mixtures of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems at finite temperature is computationally hard; identifying structural properties that enable efficient simulation is crucial.
method: The authors use cluster expansion and combinatorial arguments to show that the Gibbs state can be expressed as a mixture of Gaussian states with positive weights.
result: They prove that for sufficiently high temperature, the Gibbs state of any bounded-degree fermionic Hamiltonian is a mixture of Gaussian states, and provide explicit bounds on the temperature threshold.
conclusion: This result implies that high-temperature fermionic Gibbs states can be efficiently simulated classically, and it explains the sudden death of entanglement observed in such states.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even in the presence of noise, circumventing no-go theorems.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise, and standard quantum error correction (QEC) imposes stringent requirements that are often impractical. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using ICO.
method: The protocol employs a quantum switch to create a superposition of causal orders for error correction operations, effectively canceling noise without the need for active QEC or precise control.
result: The ICO-based scheme achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling for frequency estimation under various noise models, including dephasing and amplitude damping, with significantly relaxed experimental requirements.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a practical and noise-resilient approach to Heisenberg-limited sensing, offering a new pathway for quantum metrology in realistic noisy environments.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile entanglement preservation with local discrimination.
method: They construct a protocol using sequential local measurements and classical communication, analyzing the trade-off between discrimination success and entanglement preservation.
result: They prove that for certain orthogonal bipartite states, sequential local discrimination can be performed while maintaining unbounded entanglement between the parties.
conclusion: Sequential local operations can sustain entanglement indefinitely, challenging the conventional wisdom that local discrimination necessarily consumes entanglement.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected despite one wave packet being hidden.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon is fundamental for reconciling quantum mechanics with general relativity and for potential applications in quantum information with relativistic settings.
method: The authors analyze a bipartite quantum state of two wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use entanglement witnesses and partial transpose criteria to determine separability.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected even when one party is beyond the event horizon, provided the initial state is sufficiently entangled and the detection is performed before the infalling packet crosses the horizon.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon, which has implications for black hole information paradox and relativistic quantum information protocols.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states using stabilizer channels, unifying and extending previous distillation protocols.
motivation: Resource states like maximally entangled or private states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography but are degraded by noise; distillation protocols are needed to recover high-quality states.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be efficiently characterized, and show how to design distillation protocols based on them, analyzing their performance using stabilizer formalism.
result: They demonstrate that stabilizer channels can achieve optimal distillation rates for certain resource states and provide explicit protocols that outperform existing methods.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic way to construct and analyze distillation protocols, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by the maximum work extractable via unitary operations (ergotropy). Daemonic ergotropy, which includes information gained from measurements, can exceed standard ergotropy, but the gap between them has been a challenge. The authors aim to bridge this gap using a single auxiliary charger.
method: The authors consider a quantum battery collectively time-evolved with an auxiliary charger, then extract energy by tracing out the charger. They define the difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum ergotropy as the 'daemonic gap' and show it can be bridged by optimizing the initial state and interaction.
result: They find that by using a single auxiliary charger and optimizing the protocol, the daemonic gap can be closed, allowing the battery to be charged to its maximum possible energy. The protocol works for multimode batteries and is robust to certain imperfections.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to enhance quantum battery charging using daemonic advantage, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and energy storage at the quantum scale.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Relaxation And Quantum Mpemba Effect In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Emerson Lima Caldas And Diego Paiva Pires
abstract:
Author(s): Emerson Lima Caldas and Diego Paiva Pires

The Mpemba effect happens when a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster than a system closer to equilibrium. The authors study the relaxation of systems whose effective dynamics are described by Davies maps, providing a framework to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect in Markovian open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012418] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that open quantum systems described by Davies maps can exhibit an exponentially accelerated relaxation and a quantum Mpemba effect, where a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster.
motivation: The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one; understanding its quantum analog could reveal fundamental principles of quantum thermodynamics and relaxation dynamics.
method: The authors study Markovian open quantum systems governed by Davies maps, deriving conditions for the quantum Mpemba effect and analyzing the relaxation rates using spectral properties of the Lindbladian.
result: They show that under certain conditions, the relaxation can be exponentially accelerated, and the quantum Mpemba effect occurs when the initial state has a larger overlap with slow-decaying modes.
conclusion: The work provides a framework to engineer the quantum Mpemba effect in open quantum systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and potential applications in quantum thermal machines.

title: Entanglement Recovery By Reversing The Effect Of Noise In A Quantum Repeater
authors: Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, And Seung-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Sewon Jeong, Shrobona Bagchi, Jaehak Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim, Yong-Su Kim, Taeyoung Choi, and Seung-Woo Lee

We propose a method to directly recover the degree of entanglement distributed by entanglement swapping in the presence of noise. Our approach introduces a reversing operation that probabilistically undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012602] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a reversing operation to recover entanglement degraded by amplitude damping or photon loss in quantum repeaters.
motivation: Entanglement swapping in quantum repeaters suffers from noise, reducing the fidelity of distributed entanglement. Existing methods require multiple copies or complex distillation; a direct recovery method is needed.
method: Introduces a probabilistic reversing operation that undoes the effect of amplitude damping or photon loss on a single entangled pair, enabling heralded recovery of entanglement after swapping.
result: The reversing operation can restore the degree of entanglement to near-ideal levels with a certain success probability, improving the performance of quantum repeater networks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate noise in quantum repeaters, enhancing the feasibility of long-distance quantum communication.

title: Quantum Strategies To Overcome Classical Multiplexing Limits
authors: Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Tzula B. Propp, Jeroen Grimbergen, Emil R. Hellebek, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Janice van Dam, Joshua A. Slater, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Near-term quantum networks face a bottleneck due to low quantum communication rates. This degrades performance both by lowering operating speeds and increasing qubit storage time in noisy memories, making some quantum internet applications infeasible. One way to circumvent this bottleneck is multipl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012603] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes quantum strategies using multiplexing and entanglement to overcome classical multiplexing limits in near-term quantum networks, improving communication rates.
motivation: Near-term quantum networks suffer from low communication rates, which degrade performance and make some quantum internet applications infeasible. Classical multiplexing cannot fully address this due to quantum constraints.
method: The authors develop quantum multiplexing protocols that exploit entanglement and quantum correlations to increase the effective communication rate beyond classical limits, analyzing performance under realistic noise and memory constraints.
result: The quantum strategies achieve higher throughput and lower error rates compared to classical multiplexing, demonstrating a clear quantum advantage for network communication.
conclusion: Quantum multiplexing offers a practical path to enhance near-term quantum network performance, making quantum internet applications more feasible.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on nonequilibrium work.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium thermodynamics but requires detailed knowledge of work distributions; a simpler inequality could be more practical for complex systems.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using functional integral methods and apply them to dissipative systems described by Langevin dynamics and field theories.
result: They obtain inequalities that bound the average exponentiated work in terms of equilibrium free energy differences, valid for a wide class of nonequilibrium processes.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities extend the applicability of Jarzynski-type relations to systems where the full equality is difficult to verify, offering a robust tool for nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations via thermodynamic length in far-from-equilibrium stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking; this work aims to connect fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations through the concept of thermodynamic length.
method: Derives a general expression for thermodynamic length in stochastic thermodynamics and shows how it relates to both fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
result: Establishes a unified perspective linking thermodynamic length, fluctuation relations, and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, providing new bounds on current fluctuations.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length serves as a unifying concept in stochastic thermodynamics, offering deeper insight into far-from-equilibrium processes.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their impact on repeater protocols needs systematic study.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, considering realistic noise and loss. They analyze the entanglement generation rate and fidelity as functions of the number of modes and other parameters.
result: Multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity. The optimal number of modes depends on the specific repeater architecture and noise levels.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing practical long-distance quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks, identifying efficient transmission regimes and limitations due to squeezing-induced excitations.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer new ways to control quantum correlations.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional coupling and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They find a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantify how excess excitations from strong squeezing limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the cavity-spin coupling via optical spectroscopy and coherence measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, demonstrating strong coupling between a single spin and cavity mode, with enhanced photon emission into the cavity mode.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building quantum network nodes with high entanglement rates and fidelities, advancing practical quantum repeaters.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, which has implications for understanding quantum resources.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: They identify that many phenomena considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures.
conclusion: The work advances foundational understanding of quantumness and may guide the development of quantum technologies by identifying hidden quantum resources.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and superradiance/subradiance to create steady-state entanglement.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized, with applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological matter engineering.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for robust entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, advancing quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive schemes could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors design a bosonic code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives without active measurements, and experimentally demonstrate it in a superconducting cavity.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform physical qubits, offering a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced complexity.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurement outcomes are recorded, in contrast to the power-law decay without recording. This reveals a new phase of information preservation.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes can dramatically extend the lifetime of quantum information, offering a practical strategy for error mitigation in near-term quantum devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a significant challenge for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To realize scalable quantum networks, compact and efficient interfaces between stationary qubits (neutral atoms) and flying photons are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fiber coupling on a chip, enabling high-efficiency photon collection from trapped neutral atoms.
result: The device demonstrates efficient photon extraction and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by providing a robust, high-efficiency atom-photon interface.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on genuine quantum resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification of non-projective measurements, and the experimental demonstration validates the theoretical approach.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: The authors model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its dynamics using stochastic thermodynamics and information theory. They derive trade-off relations between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental thermodynamic bound on the performance of quantum detectors.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational understanding of the thermodynamic cost of information in quantum systems, with implications for the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and measurement devices.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing high-resolution spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion, linewidths, and coherence times under various conditions.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, including charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce sensitivity to certain noise sources, achieving improved spectral stability.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show promise for quantum networking, with identified pathways to further reduce decoherence and achieve transform-limited linewidths.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scalable entanglement generation in solid-state spin ensembles is challenging due to inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. This work aims to overcome these obstacles to enable large cluster states for quantum networking.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and collective enhancement.
result: They demonstrate that the framework can generate large cluster states with sublinear experimental overhead, achieving high fidelity for up to 100 qubits.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward scalable quantum networks using solid-state spin emitters, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the stability and decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on the stability of logical information under partial measurements and the statistics of logical measurements.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating practical device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum security devices by realizing a self-testing quantum random number generator on a photonic chip, which provides provable randomness without trusting the devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip generates certified randomness with a high rate, demonstrating the feasibility of chip-scale device-independent quantum randomness expansion.
conclusion: This work paves the way for compact, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness generation on a photonic platform.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes and optimized asymmetric geometries to improve quantum repeater performance and feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-inefficient or difficult to implement. The authors aim to enhance loss tolerance and reduce resource overhead.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for tree-codes and introduce asymmetric code geometries that balance loss tolerance and resource usage. Performance is analyzed through numerical simulations.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly improve the secret key rate and reduce the required number of emitters compared to symmetric tree-codes, making near-term quantum repeaters more feasible.
conclusion: The proposed tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new opportunities for spin qubits with long coherence times and efficient readout.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, demonstrating small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits a 4-ms spin coherence time and high-fidelity single-shot readout, with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, making it suitable for quantum information processing.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, offering long coherence and high readout fidelity.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization data, allowing for practical security bounds.
result: Provides a rigorous method to translate device characterization into security parameters, enabling standards and certification.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, making QKD security proofs more applicable to real-world devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the feasibility of scalable superconducting quantum processors.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high-rate key distribution. This review consolidates the state of the art to guide future research.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, entanglement-based schemes, and quantum networks, discussing theoretical security proofs, practical implementations, and challenges like finite-size effects and composable security.
result: CV quantum communication has achieved experimental demonstrations over long distances and is competitive with discrete-variable systems in terms of key rates and security. The review highlights recent advances in high-rate CV-QKD and network architectures.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a mature and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work needed to improve security proofs and integrate with quantum repeaters.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements achieving the ultimate precision limits.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces a fundamental challenge due to incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, obscuring the ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the trade-off and derives the optimal measurement strategy using information-theoretic tools.
result: They provide a precise characterization of the minimal trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurements that saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of multiparameter estimation limits and offers practical guidance for designing experiments.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting the dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor using a scattering matrix approach.
result: A geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation is derived and verified in a quantum dot system.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between noise and geometry in nonlinear quantum transport, with implications for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States Of Continuous Variable Systems
authors: Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, And Jordi Tura
abstract:
Author(s): Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, and Jordi Tura

Continuous-variable quantum systems are foundational to quantum computation, communication, and sensing. While traditional representations using wave functions or density matrices are often impractical, the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics provides an accessible alternative by associating qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020201] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonparametric learning method for continuous-variable quantum states using tomographic representations.
motivation: Traditional representations of continuous-variable quantum states are often impractical; tomographic pictures offer an accessible alternative.
method: Develops a nonparametric learning approach that directly learns the tomographic representation from measurement data.
result: Demonstrates efficient learning of non-Gaussian quantum states, which are important for quantum information processing.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for characterizing continuous-variable quantum systems, advancing quantum information science.

title: Entanglement Growth From Entangled States: A Unified Perspective On Entanglement Generation And Transport
authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, and Shi-Xin Zhang

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous studies focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors numerically simulate entanglement entropy growth for various initial entangled states in MBL and random circuit models, comparing with product state dynamics.
result: They find that entanglement growth from entangled states exhibits distinct universal features, including a slower growth rate and different saturation behavior, governed by the initial entanglement structure.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, providing a unified perspective on entanglement generation and transport in quantum many-body systems.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation in relativistic relaxation processes.
motivation: Understanding how relaxation processes behave under Lorentz boosts is crucial for relativistic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author analyzes the effect of Lorentz boosts on relaxation spectra using relativistic kinetic theory and the concept of relativity of simultaneity.
result: A single relaxation mode is shown to broaden into a continuum with a width set by the maximum relative velocity between the system and the observer.
conclusion: Relaxation spectra are not simply time-dilated; they undergo a fundamental reshaping due to the relativity of simultaneity, with implications for relativistic fluid dynamics and thermodynamics.

title: Metacavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), And Tian Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), and Tian Jiang (江天)

Cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) harnesses light-matter interactions to produce nonclassical light states. However, a fundamental challenge lies in simultaneously achieving Purcell enhancement and tailored wave front control within a single cavity, due to conflicting resonator requirements. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a metacavity that simultaneously achieves Purcell enhancement and wavefront control for quantum light sources.
motivation: Cavity QED typically cannot combine Purcell enhancement with tailored wavefront control due to conflicting resonator requirements, limiting the generation of nonclassical light with desired spatial properties.
method: The authors design a metacavity integrating a photonic crystal cavity with a metasurface, enabling both high Purcell factor and arbitrary wavefront shaping in a single device.
result: They experimentally demonstrate enhanced spontaneous emission and controlled emission directionality from quantum dots embedded in the metacavity.
conclusion: The metacavity platform overcomes a fundamental limitation of cQED, offering a new route to engineer quantum light sources with custom spatial modes for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unbounded Sequence Of Observers Exhibiting Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering Via Probabilistic Projective Measurements
authors: Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, And Hui-Juan Zuo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, and Hui-Juan Zuo

Recent studies have demonstrated that coherent weak measurements allow Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering to be shared sequentially between a single Alice and multiple Bobs. Theoretically, this permits an unbounded sequence in the high-dimensional limit. In this work, we investigate whether the experi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012411] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering can be shared among an unbounded sequence of observers using probabilistic projective measurements, extending previous results with weak measurements.
motivation: Previous work demonstrated sequential sharing of EPR steering with weak measurements, but the question remained whether projective measurements could also enable an unbounded sequence. This paper aims to prove that probabilistic projective measurements can achieve the same effect.
method: The authors propose a protocol where Alice performs a projective measurement on her half of a maximally entangled pair, and each Bob performs a probabilistic projective measurement on his qubit, with the measurement outcome determining whether the next Bob can demonstrate steering. They analyze the steering robustness using a linear steering inequality and optimize the measurement angles.
result: They show that for any finite number of Bobs, there exists a set of measurement angles such that each Bob can demonstrate steering, and in the limit of high-dimensional systems, the number of Bobs can become unbounded.
conclusion: Probabilistic projective measurements can achieve unbounded sequential sharing of EPR steering, similar to weak measurements, providing a new perspective on the resources required for steering sharing.

title: Temporal Steering Of Entanglement Decay With Single-shot Control
authors: Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, And Urbasi Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Saumya Ranjan Behera, Kallol Sen, Animesh Sinha Roy, Snigdhadev Ray, Ashutosh Singh, A. R. P. Rau, and Urbasi Sinha

Entanglement in open quantum systems can vanish abruptly through entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution, posing a challenge for quantum technologies. Here, we show that the timing of a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the trajectory of entanglement deca…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012416] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a single local unitary operation can deterministically steer the trajectory of entanglement decay in open quantum systems, enabling control over entanglement sudden death.
motivation: Entanglement sudden death (ESD) under dissipative evolution poses a challenge for quantum technologies; controlling entanglement decay is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally demonstrate that the timing of a single local unitary operation can steer the entanglement decay trajectory in a bipartite system subject to amplitude damping.
result: They show that by applying a local unitary at a specific time, they can either accelerate or delay entanglement sudden death, effectively controlling the entanglement lifetime.
conclusion: This work provides a method for single-shot control of entanglement dynamics, which could be useful for quantum information processing in noisy environments.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology exploits quantum phase transitions for enhanced precision, but critical slowing down limits achievable precision within finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the Lieb-Robinson bound and the energy gap scaling near criticality.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/2} for a fixed evolution time T, independent of system size, revealing a trade-off between precision and measurement time.
conclusion: The scaling limit is fundamental and cannot be overcome by increasing system size, guiding optimal design of critical sensors.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistical learning method to verify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, reducing measurement overhead.
motivation: Verifying quantum state k-designs is crucial for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods require many measurements. A more efficient verification protocol is needed.
method: The authors use randomized measurements and a statistical learning approach to certify approximate k-designs with fewer measurement settings, leveraging the structure of random ensembles.
result: The method achieves efficient verification with provable guarantees, significantly reducing the number of measurements compared to full state tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for benchmarking random state ensembles, with applications in quantum circuit benchmarking and many-body physics.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, exploiting the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated and transferred between nuclear qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical route to implementing quantum repeaters and multi-party quantum communication using solid-state defect centers.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around the atom array, reducing blackbody radiation. They measure Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and compare with theoretical models.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are significantly extended (e.g., by an order of magnitude), directly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a practical and effective way to enhance Rydberg atom quantum processors, potentially enabling higher-fidelity gates and larger-scale quantum computation.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it tightly bounds the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and the compression rate for lossless compression.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and minimal disturbance remains challenging.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT in this context.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques enable practical, high-performance operation of neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases, such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating long-range interactions and kinetic constraints, and analyze its steady-state and dynamical properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new mechanism for stabilizing non-thermal states in open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays as a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents, finite-size scaling, and dynamical protocols near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance estimation precision, achieving Heisenberg-limited scaling in some cases, and discusses experimental platforms.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route for next-generation quantum metrology, with potential applications in fundamental physics and technology.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic errors in quantum control, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often sacrifice fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to optimize the control protocol, achieving higher fidelity than standard variational approaches.
result: The proposed method yields significantly improved fidelity for various quantum systems, demonstrating a practical upgrade for quantum control.
conclusion: Weighted variational counterdiabatic driving offers a readily available enhancement for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are limited by the number of atoms that can be simultaneously coupled to a single cavity mode; multiplexing multiple cavity modes allows scaling to larger arrays.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple transverse cavity modes are used to address distinct atomic ensembles within the same cavity, leveraging spatial mode separation to perform parallel operations.
