result: The approach enables simultaneous cavity-enhanced interactions (e.g., entanglement generation, state readout) across many atoms, significantly increasing the effective processing capacity of the system.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing offers a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum processors, combining the benefits of cavity coupling with large array sizes.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: The proposed photonic simulator is highly configurable and efficient for simulating quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: This work provides a practical photonic platform for studying quantum field theories, with potential applications in quantum simulation.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and exhibits instantaneous spreading, which seems incompatible with special relativity. The author aims to resolve this apparent conflict.
method: The author reformulates the diffusion equation as a relativistic field theory, deriving a covariant diffusion equation that respects causality.
result: The resulting relativistic diffusion equation is hyperbolic and causal, eliminating instantaneous spreading and Lorentz instability.
conclusion: Diffusion processes can be described in a way consistent with special relativity, bridging non-equilibrium thermodynamics and relativistic physics.

title: Emergence Of Universality In Transport Of Noisy Free Fermions
authors: João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, and Andrea De Luca

We analyze the effects of various forms of noise on one-dimensional systems of noninteracting fermions. In the strong noise limit, we demonstrate, under mild assumptions, that the statistics of the fermionic correlation matrix in the thermodynamic limit follow a universal form described by the recen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020403] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Noisy free fermions in one dimension exhibit universal transport behavior in the strong noise limit, described by the KPZ equation.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects transport in noninteracting fermion systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the fermionic correlation matrix under various noise models and derive its statistics in the thermodynamic limit using random matrix theory and the KPZ universality class.
result: In the strong noise limit, the correlation matrix statistics follow a universal form described by the KPZ equation, independent of the specific noise model.
conclusion: Noise-induced universality emerges in free fermion transport, linking quantum transport to classical stochastic growth models.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems constantly dissipate energy, and extending this paradigm to quantum systems requires a proper description of the environment and dissipation, which is currently lacking.
method: The authors derive a general theoretical framework based on open quantum systems and master equations to model dissipation in quantum active matter, incorporating both coherent and dissipative dynamics.
result: They obtain a set of equations that describe the non-equilibrium steady states and dynamics of quantum active matter, showing how dissipation leads to directed motion and pattern formation.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter and highlights the role of dissipation in driving non-equilibrium quantum phenomena, relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Distributed Quantum Dense Coding Enhanced With Nonclassical Routing
authors: Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Pratham Hullamballi, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We propose a distributed quantum dense coding protocol that uses a control system to superpose two dense coding processes, allowing us to simultaneously and coherently encode and nonclassically route the sender's single-qubit system to two receiver laboratories. We find that dense coding with cohere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012605] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A distributed quantum dense coding protocol using a control system to superpose two dense coding processes, enabling coherent encoding and nonclassical routing of a single-qubit system to two receivers.
motivation: To enhance the capacity and flexibility of quantum communication by combining dense coding with quantum routing, potentially enabling more efficient multi-party quantum networks.
method: The protocol uses a control qubit to create a superposition of two dense coding processes, each involving a different receiver, and employs nonclassical routing to direct the sender's qubit to the appropriate receiver based on the control state.
result: The protocol achieves higher information transfer rates compared to standard dense coding or classical routing, and demonstrates the advantage of coherent superposition in quantum communication tasks.
conclusion: Distributed quantum dense coding with nonclassical routing offers a new approach to multi-party quantum communication, leveraging quantum coherence to improve performance.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models through thermodynamic principles, specifically by analyzing the role of nonequilibrium latent cycles.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework connecting nonequilibrium thermodynamics with unsupervised generative modeling, focusing on latent cycles that break detailed balance.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, accelerating sampling and improving model performance.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a useful perspective for designing and analyzing generative models, with practical implications for machine learning.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: Understanding how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior and ergodicity breaking is of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods to study the steady-state properties.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a dynamical phase transition.
conclusion: The work reveals how resetting and measurements can control ergodicity and phase transitions in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various drives, analyzing classical and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating trapped particle motion.
method: The authors model the system using a Hamiltonian that includes anharmonic trapping potentials and different driving schemes, solving the equations of motion analytically and numerically.
result: They characterize the anharmonic motion and its dependence on drive parameters, showing how nonlinearities affect the dynamics and can be controlled.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling ion motion in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over the ion's motional state to engineer arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states via a sequence of laser pulses.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating complex quantum states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates; discrete modulation can improve rates while maintaining security.
method: The authors combine discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and implement the protocol over fiber optics.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over metropolitan distances, with rigorous security guarantees against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment, especially for quantum network applications.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation. This work aims to enable such control for quantum networking and computing applications.
method: The authors couple circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation via the auxiliary system.
result: They achieve nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of the circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical tool for integrating circular Rydberg atoms into quantum networks and hybrid quantum information platforms.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, improving readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical path to higher-fidelity transmon readout, benefiting quantum computing platforms.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation without exhaustive sampling.
result: The framework successfully identifies spin environments and estimates parameters with high accuracy, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies to improve efficiency.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation tasks, particularly for hybrid quantum systems where spin ensembles are coupled to other platforms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely through optimized circuit parameters and materials.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through previous performance limits.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less known; this review aims to classify and assess them.
method: The authors categorize quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a comprehensive taxonomy and highlights limitations in security and scalability of current implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers diverse functionalities beyond QKD, but practical deployment requires overcoming security and technological challenges.

title: Exponential Linewidth Narrowing And Enhancement Of Sensitivity In Ramsey Interferometry With An Optically Thick Ensemble Of Atoms
authors: S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, And E. S. Moiseev
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, and E. S. Moiseev

Ramsey resonance is a high-resolution technique used in spectroscopy, precise measurement of time and frequency, and the creation of modern clocks. The Ramsey experiments are typically done in optically dilute samples of atoms to improve homogeneity and avoid backaction of atoms on excitation pulses…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates exponential narrowing of Ramsey resonance linewidth and enhanced sensitivity using an optically thick atomic ensemble, enabled by collective effects and coherent control.
motivation: Ramsey interferometry is a key technique for precision measurements, but its resolution is typically limited by inhomogeneous broadening and optical dilution. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using an optically thick ensemble.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally study Ramsey interferometry in an optically thick ensemble of rare-earth ions, exploiting collective dipole-dipole interactions and a specific pulse sequence to achieve linewidth narrowing.
result: They observe an exponential reduction in Ramsey fringe linewidth and a corresponding increase in sensitivity, scaling with the optical depth of the ensemble.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to enhance the performance of Ramsey-based sensors and clocks using dense atomic ensembles, with potential applications in quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Environment-Assisted Generation Of Non-Gaussian Wave-Packet Quantum States
authors: Maryam Khanahmadi And Klaus Mølmer
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Khanahmadi and Klaus Mølmer

Generating non-Gaussian states and converting them into traveling wave packets is crucial yet challenging for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing. We present a hardware-efficient approach that simultaneously achieves both tasks by combining an engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-efficient method to generate non-Gaussian wave-packet quantum states using engineered nonlinear dissipation and linear transmission.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but challenging to generate and convert into traveling wave packets.
method: The approach combines engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear transmission line to simultaneously generate and shape non-Gaussian states.
result: The method produces non-Gaussian wave-packet states suitable for quantum information processing.
conclusion: This hardware-efficient technique offers a practical path to scalable quantum computing by simplifying state generation and conversion.

title: Spectrally Uniform Continuous-Variable Quantum Microcombs
authors: Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum microcombs generated in high-[MATH] microresonators provide compact, frequency-multiplexed sources of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing. Although deterministic Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing has been demonstrated on chip, achieving uniform s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates spectrally uniform continuous-variable quantum microcombs in high-Q microresonators, providing a compact frequency-multiplexed source of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing.
motivation: To achieve uniform squeezing across multiple frequency modes in on-chip CV quantum microcombs, which is essential for scalable quantum networks and information processing.
method: The authors use a high-Q microresonator with optimized dispersion and pump conditions to generate Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing with spectral uniformity.
result: They demonstrate deterministic two-mode squeezing with uniform spectral properties across multiple frequency channels, enabling frequency-multiplexed entanglement.
conclusion: Spectrally uniform CV quantum microcombs offer a practical path toward integrated, scalable quantum networks and frequency-multiplexed quantum communication.

title: Doubling Qubits In A Trapped-ion System Via Vibrational Dual-rail Encoding
authors: Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, And Joonsuk Huh
abstract:
Author(s): Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, and Joonsuk Huh

Vibrational modes of trapped ions have traditionally served as quantum buses to mediate entanglement between internal qubits. However, with recent advances in quantum control, it has become possible to use these modes directly as quantum computational resources. Here, we propose a dual-rail encoding…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a dual-rail encoding using vibrational modes of trapped ions to double the number of qubits without increasing ion count.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum computers face scalability limits due to the number of ions required. Using vibrational modes as qubits can increase computational resources without adding more ions.
method: The authors propose encoding qubits in the vibrational modes of trapped ions using a dual-rail scheme, where each ion's motional states represent logical qubits, and they analyze the required quantum control techniques.
result: The dual-rail encoding effectively doubles the number of qubits available in a trapped-ion system, with potential for further scaling.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to increase qubit count in trapped-ion platforms, leveraging existing control capabilities.

title: Multiphoton Interference With A Symmetric Su($n$) Beam Splitter And The Generalization Of The Extended Hong-Ou-Mandel Effect
authors: Paul M. Alsing, Richard J. Birrittella, And Peter L. Kaulfuss
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Alsing, Richard J. Birrittella, and Peter L. Kaulfuss

We examine multiphoton interference with a symmetric [MATH] beam splitter [MATH], an extension of features of the [MATH] 50/50 beam splitter extended Hong-Ou-Mandel (eHOM) effect, whereby one obtains a zero amplitude (probability) for the output coincidence state (defined by e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012409] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes the extended Hong-Ou-Mandel effect to symmetric SU(n) beam splitters, analyzing multiphoton interference and zero-amplitude output conditions.
motivation: Understanding multiphoton interference in higher-dimensional beam splitters is important for quantum information processing and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.
method: The authors use group-theoretic and combinatorial methods to derive conditions for zero-amplitude coincidence states in symmetric SU(n) beam splitters, extending the known SU(2) results.
result: They find that the extended Hong-Ou-Mandel effect generalizes to SU(n) with specific input states, leading to complete destructive interference for certain output configurations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for multiphoton interference in symmetric multiport devices, with potential applications in quantum computing and communication.

title: Quantum Resource Theory Of $π$-ordered Coherence
authors: Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, And Jinchuan Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofei Qi, Bing Xu, Zhijie Wang, and Jinchuan Hou

Within the framework of resource theory, the research on quantum coherence has not only furnished a rigorous and systematic methodology for investigating quantum coherence and developing coherence quantification methods, but also tackled key issues regarding the conversion and practical utilization …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012417] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for π-ordered coherence, a specific type of quantum coherence, and provides a complete set of conditions for state transformations under free operations.
motivation: Quantum coherence is a key resource in quantum information, but most resource theories focus on standard coherence. The authors aim to extend the framework to π-ordered coherence, which arises in certain physical contexts.
method: The paper defines free operations and states for π-ordered coherence, then characterizes the preorder of state convertibility using majorization-like conditions. It also introduces measures of π-ordered coherence.
result: A complete set of necessary and sufficient conditions for converting one π-ordered coherent state to another via free operations is obtained, along with a family of monotones that quantify the resource.
conclusion: The resource theory of π-ordered coherence is fully characterized, providing a rigorous framework for studying this type of coherence and its potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Collective Vibronic Cascade In Cavity-coupled Jahn-Teller Active Molecules
authors: Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, And Krishna R. Nandipati
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Kumar Pandit, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar, and Krishna R. Nandipati

We study the polaritonic states and dynamics of multiple Jahn-Teller (JT) active molecules coupled to the modes of a Fabry-Perot cavity. We find that collective effects dramatically alter the interplay of electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta, giving rise to markedly different polarito…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012802] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective vibronic cascades in cavity-coupled Jahn-Teller active molecules, revealing how collective effects modify polaritonic states and dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the interplay of electronic, vibrational, and cavity angular momenta in molecular systems coupled to optical cavities is crucial for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze multiple Jahn-Teller active molecules coupled to Fabry-Perot cavity modes, using a model that incorporates collective effects and angular momentum coupling.
result: Collective effects dramatically alter the polaritonic states, leading to markedly different dynamics compared to single-molecule or uncoupled scenarios.
conclusion: The work provides insights into hybrid quantum systems where molecular vibrations and cavity photons interact, relevant for quantum networking and transduction.

title: Nonequilibrium (thermo)dynamics Of Colloids Under Mobile Piston Compression
authors: Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, And Joachim Dzubiella
abstract:
Author(s): Arturo Moncho-Jordá, José López-Molina, and Joachim Dzubiella

We investigate the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile boundary within dynamical density functional theory. The system consists of a hard-sphere fluid confined between two parallel walls, one of which acts as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015403] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium compression of a confined colloidal fluid driven by a mobile piston using dynamical density functional theory.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamics and dynamics of soft matter under nonequilibrium conditions is important for both fundamental physics and applications like microfluidics.
method: The authors employ dynamical density functional theory (DDFT) to model a hard-sphere fluid confined between two walls, with one wall acting as an overdamped piston subjected to a sudden increase in external force.
result: They find that the piston motion and fluid density profiles exhibit complex relaxation dynamics, with the system's free energy and pressure showing non-monotonic behavior during compression.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of colloidal systems under mechanical driving, relevant to information thermodynamics and soft matter physics.

title: Score-based Modeling Of Effective Langevin Dynamics
authors: Ludovico Theo Giorgini
abstract:
Author(s): Ludovico Theo Giorgini

We introduce a constructive framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series. Unlike conventional approaches that require iterative calibration to match target statistics, our construction guarantees the observed steady-state density by design and enforces short-lag coordi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A framework to learn effective Langevin equations from stationary time series that guarantees the observed steady-state density by design.
motivation: Conventional approaches require iterative calibration to match target statistics; this work aims to provide a more direct and principled method.
method: The authors construct a score-based model that enforces the observed steady-state density and short-lag correlations, learning the drift and diffusion terms of an effective Langevin equation.
result: The method yields accurate effective dynamics that reproduce the stationary distribution and correlation functions of the original system.
conclusion: This framework offers a practical tool for modeling complex stochastic systems, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation leads to distinct transport behavior.
motivation: Understanding how the quantum statistics of a bath (fermionic vs. spin) affects transport in open quantum systems is important for modeling realistic environments.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to analyze transport through a single site coupled to either a fermionic reservoir or a bath of spin modes.
result: Fermionic anticommutation suppresses transport compared to the spin bath, and the difference persists even in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The choice of bath statistics qualitatively impacts transport, which must be accounted for in open quantum system models.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Förster resonance to achieve high sensitivity.
motivation: Electric field sensing with high spatial resolution is important for various applications; Rydberg atoms offer strong field dependence near Förster resonances.
method: The sensor uses a network of Rydberg atoms where the blockade radius depends on the local electric field; variations in the field cause changes in the excitation pattern, which can be read out.
result: The scheme achieves sub-mV/cm sensitivity with micrometer spatial resolution, and the network geometry can be optimized for different sensing tasks.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks provide a promising platform for electric field gradiometry with high sensitivity and spatial resolution.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed optical states by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate and exploiting nonlinear atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and metrology, but generating it in a compact, integrated platform remains challenging. This work aims to leverage atomic nonlinearities in a BEC for on-demand squeezing.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective atomic spin excitation in a BEC. During storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved optical mode.
result: The scheme predicts significant squeezing (e.g., 3 dB) under realistic experimental parameters, with the squeezing level tunable via storage time and atomic density.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a new route to generate squeezed light using cold atoms, potentially enabling compact, integrated sources for quantum technologies.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum synchronization in a controlled platform, which is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators and measuring their relative phase.
result: Synchronization is observed through a fixed relative phase accessible only via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental realization of quantum synchronization, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, providing a practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum systems.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful and scalable method for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system and quantifies the advantage via cross-entropy benchmarking.
result: The processor achieves a computational task that is infeasible for classical supercomputers, demonstrating a utilizable quantum advantage.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating quantum computational advantage in practical settings.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their generation and readout using cavity-mediated interactions.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming classical and other entangled states in realistic noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks with enhanced robustness, making them promising for next-generation quantum metrology.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump process theories.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables in systems with both diffusive and jump-like dynamics.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics in complex systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is relevant to understanding qubit leakage in superconducting qubits.
motivation: Transmon ionization can cause qubits to leak out of the computational subspace, degrading gate fidelity and readout accuracy. Understanding this process is crucial for improving qubit performance.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize the excited-state dynamics of transmon qubits, identifying multiphoton resonances that lead to ionization.
result: They observe clear signatures of Landau-Zener transitions and quantify the ionization rates under various drive conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the mechanisms of transmon ionization, which can inform the design of better readout schemes and error mitigation strategies.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Improving displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions, leveraging the nonlinear spin-motion coupling to create squeezed states that enhance displacement sensitivity.
result: They show that the proposed scheme achieves the Heisenberg limit for displacement sensing, outperforming standard quantum limit approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to extend the reach of such simulations by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop techniques to reduce the number of stabilizer terms in the decomposition of unitary operators by exploiting strong and weak symmetries, making the simulation of multiqubit unitaries tractable beyond previous limits.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reduction renders optimal stabilizer decompositions feasible for larger circuits, significantly improving simulation efficiency for Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of quantum circuits with moderate non-Clifford resources, aiding in the verification of near-term quantum devices.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to experimental imperfections and crosstalk.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints and minimizing gate errors.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary operators into unitary operations on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods, enabling efficient simulation of linear differential equations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, advancing quantum algorithms for differential equations.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling detection of correlated noise sources.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency range, providing new insights into noise mechanisms affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve robust photon blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases, even with weak individual couplings.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics at the few-photon level.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum simulators more practical for large-scale quantum simulation tasks.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a theoretical framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for the loss function in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise strength. They use tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a trade-off between noise and trainability. Quantitative estimates for the loss function concentration are provided.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit structure, potentially improving the training of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, where the Hamiltonian simulation step uses randomized product formulas that trade determinism for lower circuit depth and gate count, while maintaining sufficient accuracy for phase estimation.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic product formulas, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution is a practical technique to slash the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain classes of problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, compares their query complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; the survey identifies open problems and future directions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic approaches, and tensor network methods.
conclusion: The unified framework helps relate different approaches and guides the choice of method for specific applications in quantum thermodynamics and information.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum circuits, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve the efficiency of quantum algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, though challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various solid-state spin qubits, discussing challenges for higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for complex environments.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly accurate, aiding the design of better spin qubits for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Robust Negativity In The Quantum-to-classical Transition Of Kerr Dynamics
authors: Mohsin Raza, John B. Debrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, And Ivan H. Deutsch
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsin Raza, John B. DeBrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, and Ivan H. Deutsch

We quantify the quantum-to-classical transition of the single-mode Kerr nonlinear dynamics in the presence of loss. We establish three timescales that govern the dynamics, each with distinct characteristics. For times short compared with the Ehrenfest time, the evolution is classical, characterized …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013708] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies the quantum-to-classical transition in Kerr nonlinear dynamics under loss, establishing three distinct timescales and showing that negativity is robust against moderate loss.
motivation: Understanding the quantum-to-classical transition is fundamental to quantum information processing, and Kerr dynamics provide a rich testbed for studying decoherence and the loss of quantum features.
method: The authors analyze the single-mode Kerr Hamiltonian with photon loss using phase-space methods and negativity of the Wigner function as a quantumness measure, deriving analytical expressions for three characteristic timescales.
result: They identify three timescales: Ehrenfest time, negativity decay time, and classical recurrence time, and show that negativity persists beyond the Ehrenfest time even with moderate loss.
conclusion: The robustness of negativity suggests that quantum effects in Kerr dynamics can survive significant decoherence, which is relevant for quantum information protocols using nonlinear optical systems.

title: Tunneling Of Bosonic Qubits Under Local Dephasing Through A Microscopic Approach
authors: Alberto Ferrara, Farzam Nosrati, Andrea Smirne, Jyrki Piilo, And Rosario Lo Franco
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Ferrara, Farzam Nosrati, Andrea Smirne, Jyrki Piilo, and Rosario Lo Franco

We present a microscopic derivation of a master equation for two-component bosons (bosonic qubits) which tunnel between spatially separated modes under local dephasing noise. Starting from the full system-bath Hamiltonian with Lorentzian coupling distributions, we analytically obtain a time-local ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012415] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic master equation for bosonic qubits tunneling under local dephasing is derived, revealing non-Markovian effects and qubit dynamics.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in bosonic qubits is crucial for quantum information processing; a microscopic approach captures non-Markovian effects often missed by phenomenological models.
method: Starting from a full system-bath Hamiltonian with Lorentzian coupling, the authors analytically derive a time-local master equation for two-component bosons tunneling between spatially separated modes under local dephasing.
result: The derived master equation shows that local dephasing can induce non-Markovian dynamics and affect tunneling coherence, with analytical expressions for the decoherence rates.
conclusion: The microscopic model provides a more accurate description of bosonic qubit decoherence, which is important for designing robust quantum information protocols.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient method to classically simulate small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding the structure of expectation landscapes is crucial for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly. The authors aim to efficiently surrogate local patches of these landscapes.
method: They develop a classical surrogate model that approximates expectation values in a local region by leveraging a small amount of quantum measurement data, using techniques from classical shadow tomography and polynomial approximation.
result: The method achieves accurate predictions for local patches with a sample complexity that scales favorably with system size, enabling efficient classical simulation of subregions.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum and classical computation for variational algorithms, potentially reducing quantum resource requirements while maintaining accuracy in local landscape exploration.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, including operator growth.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics beyond training data.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure of Floquet systems.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth for several model systems, generalizing to unseen driving parameters.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A technique for dynamical decoupling using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or are not tailored to correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling device-tailored sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, offering efficient protection against spatially correlated errors.
