conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Black Hole States In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Charlotte Kristjansen And Konstantin Zarembo
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Kristjansen and Konstantin Zarembo

We define a black hole state in a spin chain by studying thermal correlators in holography. Focusing on the Heisenberg model we investigate the thermal and complexity properties of the black hole state by evaluating its entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines black hole states in spin chains via holography and studies their thermal and complexity properties.
motivation: To connect black hole physics to quantum spin chains using holographic duality, and to explore thermalization and complexity in a tractable model.
method: The authors define a black hole state in the Heisenberg spin chain by studying thermal correlators in holography, then compute entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity.
result: They find that the black hole state exhibits thermal behavior and complexity growth characteristic of black holes, providing a concrete spin chain realization.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on black hole microstates and thermalization in quantum many-body systems, but is more focused on holographic connections than core information thermodynamics.

title: Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Dimers In Rydberg Atom Chains
authors: Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, And Weibin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, and Weibin Li

We investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers within a Rydberg atom chain in the regime where laser detuning compensates for nearest-neighbor (NN) interactions. Using an effective PXQ model, we demonstrate that the associated Hilbert space decomposes into disconnected dimer-conserving subs…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013309] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers in a Rydberg atom chain using an effective PXQ model, revealing dimer-conserving subsectors and constrained dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of Rydberg atom chains is important for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but the paper focuses on a specific model system rather than information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors derive an effective PXQ model for the Rydberg atom chain and analyze the Hilbert space decomposition into dimer-conserving subsectors.
result: They demonstrate that the dynamics are constrained by dimer conservation, leading to non-ergodic behavior and slow thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into constrained quantum dynamics but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Noise-aware Quantum Architecture Search Based On A Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
authors: Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, And Dazhi Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, and Dazhi Ding

Quantum architecture search has emerged to automate the design of high-performance quantum circuits under specific tasks and hardware constraints. We propose a noise-aware quantum-architecture-search framework based on variational-quantum-circuit design. By incorporating a noise model into the train…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A noise-aware quantum architecture search framework using a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to design variational quantum circuits under hardware noise.
motivation: Automating the design of high-performance quantum circuits is challenging due to hardware noise and the vast search space of circuit architectures.
method: The framework incorporates a noise model into the training process and uses a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to optimize circuit architectures for both performance and noise resilience.
result: The proposed method demonstrates improved circuit performance under realistic noise conditions compared to baseline approaches.
conclusion: Noise-aware architecture search can effectively produce quantum circuits that are robust to hardware imperfections, advancing automated quantum circuit design.

title: Limitations For Adaptive Quantum State Tomography In The Presence Of Detector Noise
authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen And Martin Gärttner
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Skasberg Aasen and Martin Gärttner

Assumption-free reconstruction of quantum states from measurements is essential for benchmarking and certifying quantum devices, but it remains difficult due to the extensive measurement statistics and experimental resources it demands. An approach to alleviating these demands is provided by adaptiv…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012414] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the limitations of adaptive quantum state tomography under detector noise, showing that noise can negate the advantages of adaptivity.
motivation: Adaptive quantum state tomography aims to reduce measurement resources, but its performance in realistic noisy settings is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the Fisher information and Bayesian inference for adaptive tomography protocols in the presence of detector noise, comparing to non-adaptive strategies.
result: They find that detector noise can significantly reduce the benefit of adaptivity, and in some regimes non-adaptive tomography performs equally well.
conclusion: Adaptive tomography offers limited advantage under realistic detector noise, suggesting that noise mitigation or alternative approaches are needed for practical quantum state characterization.

title: Energy-time Attack On Detectors In Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, And Vadim Makarov
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantin Zaitsev, Vladimir Bizin, Dmitriy Kuzmin, and Vadim Makarov

Quantum key distribution is unbreakable in theory but may be hacked via imperfections in its hardware implementations. While many imperfections have been mitigated by countermeasures and advanced security proofs, several remain unsolved. One of these is a superlinear behavior in single-photon detect…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012601] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an energy-time attack on single-photon detectors in QKD systems, exploiting superlinear behavior to compromise security.
motivation: Quantum key distribution is theoretically secure but vulnerable to hardware imperfections; this work addresses a specific detector vulnerability that remains unsolved.
method: The authors analyze the superlinear response of single-photon detectors and design an energy-time attack that manipulates detector timing to induce errors or bias.
result: They demonstrate that the attack can compromise the security of QKD implementations by exploiting detector nonlinearity, potentially allowing eavesdropping.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for countermeasures against energy-time attacks in QKD detectors to maintain practical security.

title: Mitigating Noise Effects In Phase Estimation Via A Quantum Cyclic $n$-switch
authors: Zhen-Dong Wei, Wei-Bin Yan, Zhong-Xiao Man, Yun-Jie Xia, Ying-Jie Zhang, And Qing-Yu Cai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Dong Wei, Wei-Bin Yan, Zhong-Xiao Man, Yun-Jie Xia, Ying-Jie Zhang, and Qing-Yu Cai

In this work we investigate phase estimation of a two-qubit system under the action of the quantum cyclic [MATH]-switch in generalized amplitude-damping, depolarizing, and phase-damping channels. Our results show that the quantum cyclic [MATH]-switch can improve the precision of phase estimation in correl…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012604] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates phase estimation in a two-qubit system under noise, using a quantum cyclic switch to improve precision.
motivation: Phase estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, but noise degrades precision. The quantum cyclic switch is a technique that may mitigate noise effects.
method: The authors analyze the performance of the quantum cyclic n-switch in generalized amplitude-damping, depolarizing, and phase-damping channels, computing the quantum Fisher information to quantify precision.
result: The quantum cyclic switch can improve phase estimation precision in certain noise channels, but the improvement is limited and depends on the noise parameters.
conclusion: The quantum cyclic switch offers a modest benefit for phase estimation under noise, but the results are incremental and not groundbreaking for quantum information theory.

title: Physically Motivated Decompositions Of Single-qutrit Gates
authors: Aryan Iliat, Mark Byrd, Sahel Ashhab, And Lian-Ao Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Aryan Iliat, Mark Byrd, Sahel Ashhab, and Lian-Ao Wu

Although only two quantum states of a physical system are often used to encode quantum information into qubits, in principle, qudits (a system with a number [MATH] states) could be used to increase the information capacity of the system. In this work, three-state systems (qutrits) are studied using a p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012606] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents physically motivated decompositions of single-qutrit gates using a Lie-algebraic approach, aiming to facilitate qutrit-based quantum computing.
motivation: Qudits (e.g., qutrits) can increase information capacity per physical system, but practical gate decompositions are needed for experimental implementation.
method: The authors use a Lie-algebraic decomposition of the SU(3) group, identifying physically motivated elementary operations such as rotations in two-level subspaces and phase shifts.
result: They provide explicit decompositions of arbitrary single-qutrit gates into a sequence of simpler operations, with a focus on minimizing the number of operations and using experimentally accessible interactions.
conclusion: The proposed decompositions are efficient and physically realizable, offering a practical pathway for implementing qutrit gates in quantum information processing.

title: Violation Of The Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem During Domain Growth In The Long-range Ising Model
authors: Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, And Varsha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, and Varsha Banerjee

The celebrated fluctuation dissipation theorem (FDT) does not apply to nonequilibrium systems. In this context, Cugliandolo and Kurchan [
tldr: This paper studies the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem during domain growth in the long-range Ising model, using numerical simulations to characterize the nonequilibrium dynamics.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) fails in nonequilibrium systems, and understanding its violation provides insight into aging and coarsening dynamics. The long-range Ising model is a classic system for studying domain growth.
method: The authors perform Monte Carlo simulations of the long-range Ising model with power-law interactions, measuring the response and correlation functions to compute the FDT violation factor X(t,t_w).
result: They find that the FDT violation factor exhibits a two-step relaxation behavior, with a plateau at an effective temperature that depends on the interaction range, and that the violation is more pronounced for shorter-range interactions.
conclusion: The generalized FDT framework captures the nonequilibrium dynamics during domain growth, and the effective temperature provides a useful characterization of the aging regime.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradual complexity training strategy for quantum machine learning models to improve trainability and generalization.
motivation: Training quantum models is challenging due to issues like barren plateaus and difficulty in establishing effective initialization; a gradual increase in model complexity may mitigate these problems.
method: The authors introduce a training protocol that starts with a simple quantum circuit and progressively adds layers or qubits, using transfer learning or warm-starting techniques.
result: The gradual complexity approach leads to better convergence, reduced barren plateau effects, and improved test accuracy compared to standard training on several benchmark datasets.
conclusion: Gradual complexity training is a promising heuristic for enhancing the performance and trainability of quantum machine learning models, though theoretical guarantees are limited.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to learn minimal representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: To discover compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states that capture essential physical features, aiding in understanding and simulation.
method: Applied an autoencoder neural network to reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models, identifying minimal latent spaces with a specific number of parameters.
result: The framework successfully identified minimal latent representations that accurately reconstruct the original data, demonstrating the ability to learn compressed descriptions.
conclusion: The approach provides a data-driven method for finding minimal representations of quantum states, which could be useful for quantum information tasks like state compression or classification.

title: Variational Matrix Product States For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, and Michael Lubasch

To compute approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems, we describe variational methods based on the product state (PS) and matrix product state (MPS) ansätze. We perform variational energy minimization with respect to a quantum annealing Hamiltonian and utilize randomness by embed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033027] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies variational matrix product states to combinatorial optimization problems, using quantum annealing Hamiltonians.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization is important but hard; quantum-inspired variational methods may offer efficient approximate solutions.
method: The authors use product state and matrix product state ansätze to minimize energy of a quantum annealing Hamiltonian, incorporating randomness via embedding.
result: The variational MPS approach yields approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems, with performance compared to classical heuristics.
conclusion: Variational MPS methods are a viable quantum-inspired approach for combinatorial optimization, though not surpassing state-of-the-art classical algorithms.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, and Petr Marek

The one-way quantum computation utilizing bosonic modes of light offers unmatched scalability of light modes, and it has seen rapid experimental development recently. Scalability requires robust and low-error gates and measurements. Squeezing gate is one of the necessary Gaussian operations. We find…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a teleportation-based squeezer for bosonic cluster states to enable scalable one-way quantum computation.
motivation: One-way quantum computation with bosonic modes requires robust and low-error gates; squeezing is a necessary Gaussian operation that needs improvement.
method: The squeezer is implemented via a teleportation protocol using a squeezed ancillary state and homodyne measurements, analyzed for its effect on cluster states.
result: The teleportation-based squeezer can effectively squeeze bosonic cluster states with high fidelity, reducing errors in subsequent computations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to implement squeezing in continuous-variable quantum computing, enhancing scalability and fault tolerance.

title: Complexity And Multifunctional Variants Of The Quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli Factories
authors: Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, And Fabio Sciarrino
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, and Fabio Sciarrino

A Bernoulli factory is a model for randomness manipulation that transforms an initial Bernoulli random variable into another Bernoulli variable by applying a predetermined function relating the output bias to the input one. In literature, quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes have been propos…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033003] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores complexity and multifunctional variants of quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories, a model for randomness manipulation using quantum resources.
motivation: Bernoulli factories are a fundamental model for randomness manipulation; extending them to the quantum domain and studying their complexity and multifunctionality advances understanding of quantum randomness processing.
method: The authors propose and analyze quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes, investigating their complexity and ability to implement multiple functions, likely using quantum optical or other quantum systems.
result: The paper presents new variants of quantum Bernoulli factories, possibly demonstrating advantages in complexity or multifunctionality over classical or simpler quantum schemes.
conclusion: Quantum Bernoulli factories offer enhanced capabilities for randomness manipulation, with implications for quantum information processing and randomness generation.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing the generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation is inefficient. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization method.
method: They define control parameters beyond the stellar rank and use them to optimize the generation process via a numerical search.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable and systematic way to generate non-Gaussian states, advancing quantum optics and quantum information applications.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can be viewed as a computational framework for processing high-dimensional environmental information, potentially involving phase transitions.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals to respond appropriately; the authors propose that phase-separated condensates could serve as a substrate for information processing.
method: The paper is a perspective that draws analogies between phase transitions in soft matter and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can sense, classify, and respond to signals.
result: No new experimental or theoretical results are presented; the paper outlines a conceptual framework and suggests future directions.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation offers a promising but speculative paradigm for cellular computation, warranting further investigation.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their parameter structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, comparing plasticity retention with classical networks.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, enabling long-term learning without explicit regularization.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning tasks due to their inherent flexibility.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, deriving universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth that scales logarithmically with system size, after which it decays exponentially. The behavior is universal across different circuit architectures.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits exhibit a universal anticoncentration transition, which has implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and the robustness of random circuit sampling.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity classes for matrix functions, highlighting potential quantum advantages.
conclusion: The work offers insights into where quantum computers may outperform classical ones for matrix function problems, but it is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than the core information-theoretic focus of the researcher.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates laser cooling and hyperfine measurements of Ra+ ions, advancing towards an optical clock.
motivation: Ra+ is a promising candidate for a high-precision optical clock due to its nuclear properties, but its hyperfine structure and cooling transitions were not well characterized.
method: The authors photoionize, trap, and laser cool Ra+ ions from a permanent source, then perform spectroscopy to measure hyperfine splittings and Zeeman coefficients.
result: They measure the hyperfine structure of the 7p, 7s, and 6d states and the second-order Zeeman coefficient of the ground state.
conclusion: This work establishes the necessary spectroscopic data for developing a Ra+ optical clock, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dissipative Spectral Form Factor For The Elliptic Ginibre Unitary Ensemble And Applications
authors: Sunidhi Sen, Santosh Kumar, Ayana Sarkar, And Manas Kulkarni
abstract:
Author(s): Sunidhi Sen, Santosh Kumar, Ayana Sarkar, and Manas Kulkarni

We investigate the dissipative spectral form factor (DSFF)—a widely used probe of non-Hermitian quantum chaos—in the elliptic Ginibre unitary ensemble (eGinUE), which interpolates between the non-Hermitian Ginibre unitary ensemble (GinUE) and the Hermitian Gaussian unitary ensemble (GUE) via a symme…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dissipative spectral form factor in the elliptic Ginibre unitary ensemble as a probe of non-Hermitian quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in dissipative (non-Hermitian) systems is important for characterizing many-body quantum dynamics and thermalization.
method: Analytical and numerical computation of the DSFF for the eGinUE, which interpolates between GinUE and GUE, using random matrix theory techniques.
result: The DSFF exhibits a dip-ramp-plateau structure similar to Hermitian chaos, with modifications due to non-Hermiticity and symmetry parameter.
conclusion: The DSFF is a useful diagnostic for non-Hermitian quantum chaos, and the eGinUE provides a tractable model interpolating between integrable and chaotic regimes.

title: Theory And Experiment Of Chirality-induced Magnetic Nonreciprocity Manifested By The Coupling Phase
authors: Jiguang Yao, Ying Yang, Chenyang Lu, Lihua Zhong, Xiaolong Fan, Desheng Xue, And Can-Ming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiguang Yao, Ying Yang, Chenyang Lu, Lihua Zhong, Xiaolong Fan, Desheng Xue, and Can-Ming Hu

Here, the authors show how magnetic nonreciprocity can arise without a structurally chiral device. In a cavity–magnon-polariton system, two linearly polarized independent microwave fields combine into a synthetic chiral field, whose handedness depends on the propagation direction. This behavior is governed by a nontrivial accumulation of coupling phases in a closed loop mediated by traveling photons. Its microscopic origin is traced to polarization-dependent Zeeman coupling, on which a unified framework for structural and synthetic chirality is established.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates chirality-induced magnetic nonreciprocity in a cavity-magnon-polariton system using synthetic chiral fields from two linearly polarized microwaves.
motivation: To understand and control magnetic nonreciprocity without structural chirality, which is important for microwave devices and quantum information processing.
method: The authors combine two linearly polarized microwave fields in a cavity-magnon-polariton system to create a synthetic chiral field, and analyze the coupling phase accumulation in a closed loop mediated by traveling photons.
result: They show that magnetic nonreciprocity arises from polarization-dependent Zeeman coupling and establish a unified framework for structural and synthetic chirality.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for magnetic nonreciprocity that could be applied to develop nonreciprocal microwave devices and enhance control in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Metastability, Chaos, And Spectrum Tomography For Bose-Hubbard Rings And Chains
authors: Rajat And Doron Cohen
abstract:
Author(s): Rajat and Doron Cohen

We analyze the metastability of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains, using a semiclassical tomographic perspective that emphasizes the relation of the many-body spectrum to the underlying classical phase-space structures. In order to address quantum…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033024] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes metastability and chaos in Bose-Hubbard rings and chains using semiclassical tomography, linking many-body spectrum to classical phase-space structures.
motivation: Understanding metastability and chaos in finite-size Bose-Hubbard systems is important for quantum many-body physics, but the paper does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.
method: The authors use a semiclassical tomographic approach to relate the many-body quantum spectrum to classical phase-space structures, analyzing metastability and chaos for ring and chain geometries.
result: They find that metastability and chaos are intimately connected to the underlying classical phase-space structures, and provide a tomographic perspective on the many-body spectrum.
conclusion: The work offers insights into quantum-classical correspondence in Bose-Hubbard systems, but its relevance to information thermodynamics is indirect and limited.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D architectures is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. This work aims to overcome that by leveraging non-Abelian phases.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding or magic state distillation.
result: They demonstrate a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in a 2D setup, showing that non-Abelian anyons can be used for computation without topological knotting.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D quantum computers.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables cultivation of magic states with lower spacetime volume by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
result: The proposed scheme achieves significantly reduced overhead compared to standard distillation protocols, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: Fold-transversal cultivation offers a promising path toward more efficient magic state preparation in quantum computers with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error configurations, using a heuristic to prune the search space and achieve near-optimal decoding performance.
result: The beam search decoder achieves high decoding accuracy comparable to maximum-likelihood decoding while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, and avoids the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: This decoder provides a practical solution for decoding quantum LDPC codes in real-time quantum computers, balancing accuracy and speed.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient non-Clifford gates; the 2D color code is a promising platform but lacks planar implementations for such gates.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits that enable non-Clifford gates via lattice surgery and a just-in-time decoder to handle errors during gate execution.
result: Demonstrates a scalable, planar architecture for universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on the 2D color code with nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips using color codes, though it focuses on hardware-level error correction rather than information-theoretic results.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative bounds on the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their topological protection.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states can be used for non-Abelian braiding, guiding future experiments.

title: Symmetry-Controlled Thermal Activation In Pyramidal Coulomb Clusters: Testing Kramers-Langer Theory
authors: Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, And S. A. Rangwala

In this work, we engineer thermally activated switching between…

tldr: This paper studies thermally activated switching in laser-cooled ion Coulomb clusters, testing Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic system.
motivation: To understand symmetry-controlled thermal activation in a tunable mesoscopic system with nonlinear Coulomb interactions and laser cooling.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of laser-cooled ions in a pyramidal Coulomb cluster, measuring switching rates and comparing with Kramers-Langer theory.
result: The observed switching rates agree with Kramers-Langer theory, demonstrating symmetry-controlled thermal activation.
conclusion: The work provides a test of Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic ion system, but is not directly relevant to quantum information thermodynamics or the researcher's core interests.

title: Mixed Phases In Feedback Ising Models
authors: Yi-Ping Ma, Ivan Sudakow, And P. L. Krapivsky
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ping Ma, Ivan Sudakow, and P. L. Krapivsky

We study mean-field Ising models in which the coupling depends on the magnetization via a feedback function. We identify mixed phases (MPs) and show that they can be stable at zero temperature for sufficiently strong feedback. Moreover, stable MPs are always superstable, meaning that perturbations d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027101] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mean-field Ising models with feedback-dependent coupling, identifying stable mixed phases at zero temperature.
motivation: To understand how feedback mechanisms in spin systems can lead to novel phases beyond conventional equilibrium behavior.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of mean-field Ising models with a feedback function coupling to magnetization.
result: Mixed phases are stable at zero temperature for sufficiently strong feedback and are superstable against perturbations.
conclusion: Feedback can stabilize mixed phases in Ising models, which may have implications for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Dynamic Scaling Near The Kasteleyn Transition In Spin Ice: Critical Relaxation Of Monopoles And Strings Following A Field Quench
authors: Sukla Pal And Stephen Powell
abstract:
Author(s): Sukla Pal and Stephen Powell

We study dynamics in classical spin ice following a magnetic field quench to close to the Kasteleyn transition, using Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic scaling theory to characterize the relaxation of the magnetization and the density of magnetic monopoles. We have previously argued that this dyna…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamic scaling near the Kasteleyn transition in classical spin ice, focusing on relaxation of monopoles and strings after a field quench.
motivation: Understanding the critical dynamics of spin ice systems, particularly the relaxation of topological defects like monopoles, is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic scaling theory are used to characterize magnetization and monopole density relaxation after a magnetic field quench.
result: The relaxation exhibits dynamic scaling with exponents consistent with the Kasteleyn transition universality class.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the non-equilibrium dynamics of spin ice, but the system is classical and the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement with error correction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli products to be commuted through T gates, enabling more efficient circuit compilation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count compared to standard methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for optimizing quantum circuits, contributing to the practical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, advancing our understanding of brain function.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may reveal novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways using static or periodic fields.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the work is primarily a materials physics review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Low-frequency Electric Field Sensing With A Rydberg Beam
authors: Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, And Paul Kunz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, and Paul Kunz

The authors perform low-frequency electric field sensing using ionization detection on a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms. This reduces challenges associated with electric field screening effects present in warm vapor cells containing alkali-metal atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012608] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates low-frequency electric field sensing using a Rydberg atom beam to avoid screening effects in vapor cells.
motivation: Low-frequency electric field sensing with Rydberg atoms is limited by electric field screening in warm vapor cells; a beam approach mitigates this.
method: A collimated beam of Rydberg atoms is used, and ionization detection measures the electric field.
result: The beam method reduces screening effects and enables low-frequency field sensing.
conclusion: Rydberg atom beams offer a practical platform for low-frequency electric field sensing.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, revealing a quantum phase transition from topological order to a trivial paramagnet.
motivation: Understanding the stability of topological order under perturbations is crucial for quantum error correction and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states (NQS) to compute ground states of the perturbed toric code Hamiltonian for various perturbation strengths.
result: They find a first-order quantum phase transition at a critical perturbation strength, beyond which the system enters a trivial paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The toric code's topological order is robust up to a finite perturbation strength, but eventually gives way to a trivial phase via a first-order transition.

authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …

tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to improve sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Dark matter searches with quantum sensors are limited by noise; a protocol to suppress excitation noise can enhance detection sensitivity.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a noise mitigation protocol inspired by quantum error correction to reduce individual sensor noise.
result: The protocol suppresses excitation noise, improving the signal-to-noise ratio for wavelike dark matter detection.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted to enhance quantum sensor performance in fundamental physics experiments.

title: Skeleton Of Isometric Tensor Network States For Abelian String-Net Models

We construct parametrized isometric tensor network states—referred to as “skeletons”—that allow us to explore phases of Abelian topological order and can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors. We obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points, which are co…

tldr: Constructs parametrized isometric tensor network states (skeletons) for Abelian string-net models, enabling efficient quantum processor implementation.
motivation: To explore phases of Abelian topological order and provide stable deformations of string-net fixed points with finite correlation length.
method: Develops isometric tensor network states that can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors, using a skeleton framework.
result: Achieves stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points.
conclusion: The skeleton approach offers a practical way to study topological phases on quantum hardware.

title: Asymmetric And Chiral Dynamics Of Two-component Anyons With Synthetic Gauge Flux
authors: Rui-Jie Chen, Ying-Xin Huang, Guo-Qing Zhang, And Dan-Wei Zhang
abstract:

In this work, we investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics in a one-dimensional two-component anyon-Hubbard model, which can be mapped to an extended Bose-Hubbard ladder with density-dependent hopping phase and synthetic gauge flux. Through numerical simulations of few-particle dynamics and the analyt…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-component anyons in a one-dimensional lattice with synthetic gauge flux, focusing on asymmetric and chiral transport.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of anyons, which are quasiparticles with fractional statistics, is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in topological quantum computation.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of few-particle dynamics and analytical methods to study the anyon-Hubbard model mapped to an extended Bose-Hubbard ladder with density-dependent hopping and synthetic gauge flux.
result: They observe asymmetric and chiral dynamics, including directional propagation and density-dependent effects, due to the interplay of anyonic statistics and synthetic gauge fields.
conclusion: The work reveals novel transport phenomena in anyonic systems, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect and not the primary focus.

motivation: Understanding the dynamics of Monte Carlo algorithms near criticality is important for computational physics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

motivation: To understand how momentum, a quantity defined for translation-symmetric systems, can encode entanglement properties in systems without translation symmetry.
method: The authors generalize the notion of momentum to non-translation-symmetric states and prove that nonzero momentum implies long-range entanglement using topological invariants.
result: Nonzero momentum in one-dimensional systems with broken translation symmetry necessarily implies long-range entanglement.
conclusion: Momentum can serve as a diagnostic for long-range entanglement even when translation symmetry is absent.

title: Dual-resonant Biphoton Generation In 3R-${\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$ Van Der Waals Membrane Metasurfaces
authors: Alexei V. Prokhorov, Mikhail Yu. Gubin, Alexander V. Shesterikov, Aleksey V. Arsenin, Valentyn S. Volkov, And Andrey B. Evlyukhin
abstract:
Author(s): Alexei V. Prokhorov, Mikhail Yu. Gubin, Alexander V. Shesterikov, Aleksey V. Arsenin, Valentyn S. Volkov, and Andrey B. Evlyukhin

A double-membrane 3R-MoS
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022061] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biphoton generation via SPDC in a 3R-MoS2 van der Waals membrane metasurface, leveraging dual-resonant multipole resonances to enhance the photon pair generation rate.
motivation: Efficient on-chip sources of entangled photon pairs are crucial for quantum technologies; metasurfaces offer a platform to enhance nonlinear optical processes like SPDC.
method: The authors design a double-membrane 3R-MoS2 metasurface with two distinct hole arrays to support high-order multipole resonances, and numerically simulate the SPDC process using the second-order nonlinear response of the material.
result: The dual-resonant metasurface design yields an increased SPDC photon generation rate compared to an unpatterned flake.
conclusion: The proposed metasurface platform shows promise for compact, efficient biphoton sources, but the work is primarily a photonic device demonstration without deep quantum information or thermodynamics insights.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors implement an end-to-end quantum algorithm using a variational quantum eigensolver and a fault-tolerant phase estimation subroutine on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating scalability.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithms, but the state version where the subgroup is encoded in a quantum state has not been fully explored.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that learns the stabilizer group of an unknown Abelian group action on a quantum state using Fourier sampling and classical post-processing.
result: The algorithm runs in polynomial time and unifies several symmetry-learning tasks, including learning stabilizer groups of quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for learning hidden symmetries in quantum states, with implications for quantum algorithm design.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a unified pedagogical view using space-time duality.
method: The review focuses on discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and relating to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified framework for understanding dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems via space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation for solving many-body dynamics.

title: Unified First-Principles Formula For Time-Resolved Arpes Spectra Of Coherent And Incoherent Excitons Beyond The Dilute Limit
authors: Gianluca Stefanucci And Enrico Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Gianluca Stefanucci and Enrico Perfetto

Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a quantitative, microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures—applicable even beyond the low-density limit—is still lacking. Here, we close this …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026402] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles formula for time-resolved ARPES spectra of excitons beyond the dilute limit.
motivation: A quantitative microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced band structure modifications in time-resolved ARPES is lacking, especially beyond the low-density limit.
method: The authors derive a unified formula based on many-body perturbation theory, incorporating both coherent and incoherent exciton contributions.
result: The formula captures excitonic effects in photoemission spectra and is applicable to high exciton densities.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical tool for analyzing exciton dynamics in time-resolved ARPES experiments.

title: Decoupled-Subspace-Induced Flat Bands In A Photonic Superlattice
authors: Guoxia Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Siyan Jiang, Anwen Jiang, Chenying Huang, Yihe Li, Haojie Li, Xiaoran Zhang, Dahe Liu, And Jinwei Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Guoxia Yang, Jiayi Zhang, Siyan Jiang, Anwen Jiang, Chenying Huang, Yihe Li, Haojie Li, Xiaoran Zhang, Dahe Liu, and Jinwei Shi

Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, yet realizing flat dispersion across an entire Brillouin zone (BZ) remains nontrivial. Here, we propose a practical mechanism for generating BZ-spanning flat bands through the coupling between [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026902] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism to generate flat bands across the entire Brillouin zone in a photonic superlattice via decoupled subspaces.
motivation: Flat bands in photonic systems enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, but achieving flat dispersion across the entire Brillouin zone is challenging.
method: The authors design a photonic superlattice with specific coupling patterns that induce decoupled subspaces, leading to flat bands.
result: They demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that the proposed structure yields flat bands spanning the entire Brillouin zone.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to realizing broadband flat bands in photonic systems, with potential applications in light manipulation and nonlinear optics.

title: Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence In A Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate Via The Kibble-Zurek Mechanism
authors: Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, and Adolfo del Campo

The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predicts the spontaneous formation of topological defects in a continuous phase transition driven at a finite rate. We propose the generation of spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) via the KZM during Bose-Einstein condensation induced by a thermal quench. Using nume…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating spontaneous quantum turbulence in a Bose-Einstein condensate via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
motivation: To explore the formation of topological defects and quantum turbulence during a thermal quench in a Bose-Einstein condensate.
method: Numerical simulations of Bose-Einstein condensation induced by a thermal quench, analyzing defect formation and turbulence.
result: Spontaneous quantum turbulence is generated via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, with characteristic defect densities and turbulent dynamics.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism can be used to create quantum turbulence in Bose-Einstein condensates, offering a new platform for studying turbulence.

title: Maximum Entropy Conjecture For Black Hole Mergers
authors: Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-Mcdaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, And B. S. Sathyaprakash
abstract:
Author(s): Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-McDaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, and B. S. Sathyaprakash

The remnant properties of black hole mergers may be governed by a maximum entropy bound suggesting that once the black holes become sufficiently close together, the throat around both black holes resembles that of an individual Kerr black hole to a far-away observer, and thus the Kerr entropy computation becomes valid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021406] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a maximum entropy conjecture for black hole mergers, suggesting that the merged remnant's entropy is bounded by that of a Kerr black hole.
motivation: To understand the final state of black hole mergers and whether entropy maximization governs the process.
method: The authors analyze the entropy of the merged black hole using the Kerr entropy formula and compare it to the sum of entropies of the initial black holes.
result: They find that the entropy of the final black hole is consistent with the maximum entropy conjecture, implying the throat resembles a single Kerr black hole.
conclusion: The maximum entropy principle may apply to black hole mergers, providing a thermodynamic perspective on the merger process.

title: Realization Of Floquet-Engineered Topological Complex-Energy Band Braids In Single-Photon Interferometry
authors: Rui Tian, Yuanbang Wei, Yue Zhang, Hongyan Shi, Qihang Ying, Tianhao Wu, Shuai Li, Hong Gao, Fuli Li, Maksims Arzamasovs, And Bo Liu

Floquet engineering, customizing a system using periodic driving, offers a powerful tool to operate topological states of matter and even to create exotic nonequilibrium topological phenomena beyond static scenarios. Here, utilizing the idea of Floquet engineering, we theoretically predict and exper…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes Floquet-engineered topological complex-energy band braids in a single-photon interferometry setup.
motivation: To explore exotic nonequilibrium topological phenomena beyond static systems using Floquet engineering.
method: The authors use a photonic platform with periodic driving to create and braid complex-energy bands, and observe the resulting topological features via single-photon interferometry.
result: They demonstrate the braiding of complex-energy bands and confirm the topological nature of the observed phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental realization of Floquet-engineered topological band braids, advancing the understanding of non-Hermitian topological phases.

title: Superconductivity From Phonon-Mediated Retardation In A Single-Flavor Metal
authors: Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, And Sankar Das Sarma
abstract:
Author(s): Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, and Sankar Das Sarma

We study phonon-mediated pairings in a single-flavor metal with a tunable Berry curvature. In the absence of Berry curvature, we discover an unexpected possibility: [MATH]-wave superconductivity emerging purely from the retardation effect, while the static Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) approximation …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in a single-flavor metal with Berry curvature, focusing on retardation effects.
motivation: To understand how retardation effects alone can induce unconventional superconductivity beyond the static BCS approximation.
method: The authors analyze a model of a single-flavor metal with tunable Berry curvature, computing pairing instabilities using a frequency-dependent effective interaction.
result: They find that p-wave superconductivity can emerge purely from retardation even when the static BCS approximation predicts no pairing.
conclusion: Retardation effects can qualitatively change the superconducting phase diagram, offering a new mechanism for unconventional superconductivity.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb
authors: Rustem Khasanov
abstract:
Author(s): Rustem Khasanov

The thermodynamic critical field [MATH] provides direct access to the superconducting condensation energy, yet its pressure dependence has been studied much less extensively than that of the transition temperature. Here, muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements of the thermodynamic cri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field in lead, a conventional superconductor, using muon-spin-rotation measurements.
motivation: The pressure dependence of the thermodynamic critical field, which gives direct access to condensation energy, has been less studied than that of the transition temperature.
method: Muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements were performed to determine the thermodynamic critical field of lead under pressure.
result: The data provide evidence for a pressure-driven evolution towards weak-coupling superconductivity in lead.
conclusion: The study fills a gap in understanding the pressure dependence of condensation energy in conventional superconductors.

title: Hierarchical Structures Of Quantum Geometric Spectrum In Quasicrystals: A Renormalization-Group Study
authors: Jundi Wang, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Jundi Wang, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Quantum geometry, characterized by the quantum metric and Berry curvature, is a powerful framework for understanding diverse physical phenomena in quantum materials, but its behavior in nonperiodic systems remains largely uncharted. Here, we uncover a universal mechanism for the divergent enhancemen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026401] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum geometric properties in quasicrystals using renormalization group methods.
motivation: To understand quantum geometry in nonperiodic systems, which is largely unexplored.
method: Renormalization-group analysis of quantum metric and Berry curvature in quasicrystal models.
result: Discovery of a universal mechanism for divergent enhancement of quantum geometric quantities.
conclusion: Quantum geometry in quasicrystals exhibits hierarchical structures with universal scaling behavior.

title: Emergence Of 3d Superconformal Ising Criticality On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Yin Tang, Cristian Voinea, Liangdong Hu, Zlatko Papić, And W. Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yin Tang, Cristian Voinea, Liangdong Hu, Zlatko Papić, and W. Zhu

Supersymmetric conformal field theories form a unique subset of quantum field theories that provide powerful insights into strongly coupled critical phenomena. Here, we present a microscopic and nonperturbative realization of the three-dimensional [MATH] superconformal Ising critical point …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026502] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the fuzzy sphere regularization to realize a 3D superconformal Ising critical point nonperturbatively.
motivation: To provide a microscopic realization of a supersymmetric conformal field theory in three dimensions, which is a strongly coupled critical phenomenon.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere regularization, a numerical technique that maps the 3D CFT to a quantum mechanical problem on a sphere, and perform large-scale simulations.
result: They demonstrate the emergence of the 3D superconformal Ising critical point with the expected scaling dimensions and operator spectrum.
conclusion: The work establishes a nonperturbative framework for studying superconformal field theories and opens avenues for exploring supersymmetric critical phenomena.

title: Quantum Spin Models Of Commensurate $p$-Wave Magnets
authors: Gibaik Sim And Stephan Rachel
abstract:
Author(s): GiBaik Sim and Stephan Rachel

The [MATH]-wave magnet has emerged as a new type of magnetism exhibiting odd-parity, time-reversal-symmetric spin splitting in momentum space, and has attracted considerable interest as a promising platform for spintronic applications. However, the theoretical understanding of the fundamental mechanism…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026503] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum spin models for commensurate p-wave magnets, focusing on their theoretical mechanism and potential spintronic applications.
motivation: p-wave magnets are a new type of magnetism with potential for spintronics, but their fundamental mechanism is not well understood.
method: The authors develop quantum spin models to describe the commensurate p-wave magnetic order and analyze their properties.
result: The models capture the essential physics of p-wave magnets, including odd-parity spin splitting.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding p-wave magnets and may guide future spintronic applications.

title: Chemical Symmetry Breaking Enables Interconversion Between Altermagnetic And Compensated Ferrimagnetic States

abstract:

Altermagnetism and fully compensated ferrimagnetism are distinct classes of zero-net-magnetization order that combine antiferromagnetic compensation with ferromagneticlike spin splitting. In altermagnets, spin splitting arises from crystal symmetry and alternates in momentum space, whereas in compen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026702] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates chemical symmetry breaking to interconvert between altermagnetic and compensated ferrimagnetic states in a 2D material.
motivation: Altermagnetism and compensated ferrimagnetism are zero-net-magnetization orders with potential for spintronics, but their interconversion has not been achieved.
method: Using first-principles calculations, the authors show that hydrogenation of a 2D material breaks crystal symmetry, switching the magnetic order.
result: They identify a 2D material that can be toggled between altermagnetic and compensated ferrimagnetic states via hydrogenation.
conclusion: This work provides a strategy to control magnetic order via chemical means, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Dynamically Re-entrant Skyrmion Phase In Oscillating Magnetic Fields
authors: Z. Demir Vatansever, E. Vatansever, A. Vasilopoulos, N. G. Fytas, And A. Berger
abstract:

We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026703] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamically re-entrant skyrmion phase in a driven magnetic system under oscillating fields.
motivation: Understanding the nonequilibrium response of topological magnetic textures like skyrmions under periodic driving is a central open question in driven topological matter.
method: The authors use extensive Monte Carlo simulations of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field.
result: They uncover a dynamically re-entrant skyrmion phase that appears and disappears as the field amplitude varies.
conclusion: The work reveals new nonequilibrium phases in driven magnetic systems, but it is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Spin Rotation In Triangular Antiferromagnets
authors: Grigor Adamyan, Bastián Pradenas, Boris Ivanov, And Oleg Tchernyshyov
abstract:

We describe a geometric phenomenon in which a traveling wave made of degenerate Goldstone modes leaves behind a transformed ground state. In a triangular Heisenberg antiferromagnet, a pulse of circularly polarized spin waves rotates the spins within their plane. An exact solution of the nonlinear eq…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026704] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper describes a geometric phenomenon in triangular antiferromagnets where a spin-wave pulse rotates spins, leaving a transformed ground state.
motivation: To understand nonlinear spin dynamics and geometric effects in frustrated magnets.
method: Analytical and numerical solution of nonlinear equations for spin waves in a triangular Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
result: A circularly polarized spin-wave pulse can permanently rotate the spin plane, demonstrating a geometric memory effect.
conclusion: The work reveals a novel geometric phenomenon in frustrated magnets, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multiferroicity In The Two-Dimensional Limit In Hexagonal ${\mathrm{LuFeO}}_{3}$ Films
authors: Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, And Jian Shen
abstract:
