Multiferroic oxides, which host coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders, are central to understanding correlated quantum phenomena. Yet, as thickness approaches the two-dimensional (2D) limit, both ferroelectricity and magnetism are generally expected to be strongly suppressed by depolarization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of multiferroicity in two-dimensional LuFeO3 films, demonstrating coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders at the monolayer limit.
motivation: Multiferroic oxides are important for understanding correlated quantum phenomena, but ferroelectricity and magnetism are expected to be suppressed in the 2D limit; this work aims to test that expectation.
method: The authors fabricate hexagonal LuFeO3 films down to monolayer thickness and characterize their ferroelectric and magnetic properties using various experimental techniques.
result: They find that both ferroelectric and magnetic orders persist in the 2D limit, contrary to theoretical predictions of suppression.
conclusion: The discovery of robust multiferroicity in 2D LuFeO3 opens new possibilities for studying correlated quantum phenomena in reduced dimensions and for potential applications in nanoelectronics.

title: Supercritical-Subcritical Correspondence, Asymmetric Effects, And Antisymmetric Corrections Near A Critical Point
authors: Xinyang Li And Yuliang Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyang Li and Yuliang Jin

The second-order phase transitions in the Ising model and liquid-gas systems share a universality class and critical exponents, despite the absence of [MATH] symmetry in the liquid-gas Hamiltonian. This discrepancy highlights a central puzzle in critical phenomena: what is the influence of asymme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027102] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical-subcritical correspondence and asymmetric effects near a critical point in the Ising model and liquid-gas systems.
motivation: To understand the influence of asymmetry in the liquid-gas Hamiltonian on critical phenomena, which is a puzzle in the universality class.
method: The authors analyze the supercritical-subcritical correspondence and derive antisymmetric corrections near the critical point.
result: They find that asymmetric effects lead to antisymmetric corrections that modify the critical behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of asymmetry in critical phenomena but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Analysis Of Collision-shift Assessments In Ion-based Clocks
authors: M. D. Barrett And K. J. Arnold
abstract:
Author(s): M. D. Barrett and K. J. Arnold

We consider background gas collision shifts in ion-based clocks. We give both a classical and quantum description of a collision between an ion and a polarizable particle with a simple hard-sphere repulsion. Both descriptions give consistent results, which shows that a collision-shift bound is deter…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013104] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes collision shifts in ion-based clocks due to background gas, providing classical and quantum descriptions.
motivation: Accurate timekeeping in ion clocks requires understanding systematic shifts, such as those from background gas collisions.
method: The authors develop classical and quantum models of ion-polarizable particle collisions with hard-sphere repulsion and compare the results.
result: Both classical and quantum descriptions yield consistent collision-shift bounds, confirming the validity of the classical approach.
conclusion: The work provides a reliable method to bound collision shifts in ion clocks, improving their accuracy.

title: Unconventional Quantum Spin Mixing Of Two Spin-1 Atoms Beyond The Single-mode Approximation
authors: Yanhong Liu, Fulin Deng, Haoxue Qiao, And Wenxian Zhang
abstract:

The single-mode approximation (SMA) has been widely employed in ultracold spinor gases, where all spin components share the same spatial mode. By adopting generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory, we achieve a relative error of [MATH] in the ground-state energy with a reduced effective H…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013307] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin mixing dynamics of two spin-1 atoms beyond the single-mode approximation using generalized Van Vleck perturbation theory.
motivation: The single-mode approximation is widely used but may fail for small systems; the authors aim to provide a more accurate description of spin mixing in ultracold spinor gases.
method: They apply generalized Van Vleck perturbation theory to derive an effective Hamiltonian that goes beyond the single-mode approximation.
result: They achieve a relative error in ground-state energy and analyze spin mixing dynamics with improved accuracy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the limitations of the single-mode approximation and provides a more precise theoretical framework for spin-1 atom pairs.

title: Phase Diagram Of Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates Trapped In Power-law And Hard-wall Potentials
authors: G. M. Kavoulakis
abstract:
Author(s): G. M. Kavoulakis

We investigate the rotational phase diagram of a quasi-two-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate confined in power-law and hard-wall trapping potentials. For weak interactions, the system undergoes discontinuous transitions between multiply quantized vortex states as the rotation …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013308] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rotational phase diagram of a weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate in power-law and hard-wall traps, focusing on transitions between multiply quantized vortex states.
motivation: Understanding vortex formation and phase transitions in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a quasi-two-dimensional condensate with power-law and hard-wall trapping potentials, computing the phase diagram as a function of rotation frequency.
result: They find discontinuous transitions between multiply quantized vortex states for weak interactions, with the phase diagram depending on the trap geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into vortex physics in Bose-Einstein condensates but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Scaling Law Linking Field And Weight Dynamic Ranges In Superoscillation
authors: Haitang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Haitang Yang

Superoscillation (SO) offers a theoretical pathway to unlimited far-field superresolution, yet the associated physical costs lack a unified quantitative scaling description. In this work, we investigate the fundamental limits of deep SO by establishing a scaling law that links the field dynamic rang…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a scaling law linking field and weight dynamic ranges in superoscillation for far-field superresolution.
motivation: Superoscillation offers a pathway to unlimited far-field superresolution, but the associated physical costs lack a unified quantitative scaling description.
method: The authors investigate fundamental limits of deep superoscillation by deriving a scaling law that connects the field dynamic range to the weight dynamic range.
result: A scaling law is established that quantifies the trade-off between field and weight dynamic ranges in superoscillation.
conclusion: The scaling law provides a unified description of physical costs in superoscillation, aiding in understanding its fundamental limits.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$-like Phase Transitions From Square Roots Of Supersymmetric Hamiltonians
authors: Jacob L. Barnett And Ramy El-Ganainy
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob L. Barnett and Ramy El-Ganainy

We introduce a general framework for realizing parity-time [MATH]-like phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems without imposing explicit [MATH] symmetry. The approach is based on constructing a Hamiltonian as the square root of a supersymmetric partner energy shifted by a consta…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013507] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for realizing PT-like phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems using square roots of supersymmetric Hamiltonians, without explicit PT symmetry.
motivation: To generalize PT-symmetric phase transitions to systems without explicit PT symmetry, broadening the applicability of non-Hermitian physics.
method: The authors construct a Hamiltonian as the square root of a supersymmetric partner Hamiltonian shifted by a constant, and analyze its spectral properties.
result: They demonstrate that such Hamiltonians exhibit PT-like phase transitions, with spontaneous symmetry breaking and exceptional points.
conclusion: The framework provides a new route to engineer non-Hermitian phase transitions in systems that are not inherently PT-symmetric.

title: Classically Tuning The Quantum Interference Of Two Photons Scattered By A Macroscopic Lossy Sphere
authors: A. Ciattoni

We investigate the quantum optical scattering of two-photon wave packets by a macroscopic lossy sphere by means of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in the form of modified Langevin noise formalism. Building on our recently developed general scattering framework, we show that under the far-field a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013707] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum interference of two photons scattered by a macroscopic lossy sphere using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how classical macroscopic objects affect quantum interference of photons, which is fundamental for quantum optics and potential applications.
method: Uses macroscopic quantum electrodynamics with modified Langevin noise formalism to model two-photon scattering from a lossy sphere.
result: Shows that under far-field conditions, the two-photon interference pattern can be tuned by classical parameters of the sphere.
conclusion: Classical macroscopic objects can control quantum interference, offering a way to manipulate quantum states via classical means.

title: Electron-molecule Scattering Via $R$-matrix Variational Algorithms On A Quantum Computer
authors: Dario Picozzi, Jonathan Tennyson, Vincent Graves, And Jimena D. Gorfinkiel
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Picozzi, Jonathan Tennyson, Vincent Graves, and Jimena D. Gorfinkiel

Electron-molecule collisions play a central role in both natural processes and modern technological applications, particularly in plasma processing. Conventional computational strategies such as the [MATH]-matrix method have been widely adopted yet encounter significant scaling challenges in treating m…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012407] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for electron-molecule scattering using the R-matrix method.
motivation: Electron-molecule collisions are important in plasma processing but classical R-matrix methods face scaling challenges for larger molecules.
method: The authors map the R-matrix variational formulation to a quantum computer, using a hybrid quantum-classical approach to solve the scattering problem.
result: The quantum algorithm demonstrates potential for exponential speedup in treating many-electron targets, though practical implementation remains challenging.
conclusion: Quantum computing may offer a route to overcome classical limitations in electron-molecule scattering calculations.

title: Efficient Privacy-preserving Training Of Quantum Neural Networks Through Ensemble Encoding Of Quantum States
authors: Gaoyuan Wang, Jonathan Warrell, And Mark Gerstein
abstract:
Author(s): Gaoyuan Wang, Jonathan Warrell, and Mark Gerstein

Quantum computing is gaining popularity due to its potential to detect complex patterns in data by leveraging unique quantum phenomena. It is particularly promising for complex data applications, such as those in biomedicine. However, in these contexts, it is often necessary to share and then aggreg…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012413] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving training method for quantum neural networks using ensemble encoding of quantum states.
motivation: Quantum machine learning on sensitive data (e.g., biomedical) requires privacy protection, but existing methods are inefficient or insecure.
method: The authors introduce an ensemble encoding scheme where multiple copies of a quantum state are used to hide individual data points, combined with differential privacy techniques.
result: The method achieves privacy guarantees with lower overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining model accuracy on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: Ensemble encoding offers a practical trade-off between privacy and utility for quantum neural network training.

title: Improved Delta-kick Cooling With Multiple Nonideal Kicks
authors: Harshil Neeraj, David C. Spierings, Joseph Mcgowan IV, Nicholas Mantella, And Aephraim M. Steinberg
abstract:
Author(s): Harshil Neeraj, David C. Spierings, Joseph McGowan IV, Nicholas Mantella, and Aephraim M. Steinberg

Delta-kick cooling is a technique employed to achieve low kinetic temperatures by decreasing momentum width at the cost of increased position width. In an ideal implementation, this method uses a harmonic potential to deliver a single near-instantaneous momentum kick. In practice, potentials that ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013101] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves delta-kick cooling for ultracold atoms by using multiple nonideal kicks to achieve lower temperatures.
motivation: Delta-kick cooling is limited by nonideal potentials; the authors aim to overcome this by using multiple kicks.
method: They theoretically and experimentally demonstrate a sequence of multiple nonideal kicks to reduce momentum spread.
result: Multiple kicks yield lower kinetic temperatures than a single kick, even with nonideal potentials.
conclusion: The technique enhances delta-kick cooling, making it more practical for experiments.

title: Barium Autoionization For Efficient Ion Trap Loading
authors: Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, And Wesley C. Campbell
abstract:
Author(s): Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, and Wesley C. Campbell

We report a theoretical and experimental investigation of autoionizing resonances from the [MATH] manifold in neutral barium for efficient loading of ion traps. Our calculations predict large resonant cross sections for many narrow autoionizing reson…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates autoionizing resonances in barium for efficient ion trap loading, focusing on atomic physics and experimental techniques.
motivation: Efficient loading of ion traps is crucial for quantum computing and sensing, but current methods are often inefficient or cause unwanted heating.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of autoionizing cross sections with experimental measurements using a barium atomic beam and laser spectroscopy.
result: They identify several narrow autoionizing resonances with large cross sections that enable efficient and low-noise ion trap loading.
conclusion: The proposed autoionization method offers a practical improvement for loading ion traps, which could benefit trapped-ion quantum platforms.

title: Probing Short-range Gravity Using Quantum Reflection
authors: J. Boynewicz And C. A. Sackett
abstract:
Author(s): J. Boynewicz and C. A. Sackett

Quantum reflection occurs when ultracold atoms are incident on a material surface with sufficiently low velocity. The reflecting matter wave can interfere with the incident wave to form a detectable pattern, and this pattern contains information about atom-surface interactions at micrometer scales. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum reflection of ultracold atoms to probe short-range gravity, which is a test of fundamental physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test gravity at micrometer scales using quantum interference effects from atom-surface interactions.
method: Ultracold atoms are reflected from a material surface; the interference pattern between incident and reflected matter waves is analyzed to extract information about atom-surface forces.
result: The interference pattern contains information about short-range gravitational interactions, enabling constraints on deviations from Newtonian gravity.
conclusion: Quantum reflection provides a sensitive probe for short-range gravity, but the work is not directly relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Emergent Quasiperiodic Order In Bose-Bose Mixtures Induced By Spin-dependent Periodic Potentials
authors: Abid Ali, Pei Zhang, Hiroki Saito, And Yong-Chang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Abid Ali, Pei Zhang, Hiroki Saito, and Yong-Chang Zhang

We study the ground-state and low-lying metastable phases of repulsive binary Bose-Einstein condensates confined in twisted, spin-dependent periodic optical lattices. For balanced mixtures, weak intercomponent interactions yield a fourfold momentum-space symmetry dictated by the lattice geometry. In…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013302] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent quasiperiodic order in Bose-Bose mixtures under spin-dependent periodic potentials.
motivation: To understand the ground-state and metastable phases of binary Bose-Einstein condensates in twisted optical lattices.
method: Theoretical analysis of repulsive binary BECs in spin-dependent periodic potentials, examining momentum-space symmetry and phase transitions.
result: Weak intercomponent interactions lead to fourfold momentum-space symmetry; stronger interactions induce quasiperiodic order.
conclusion: The system exhibits rich phase behavior with potential for simulating quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effective Theory Of Surface Oscillations In Self-bound Superfluid Droplets
authors: Jun Mitsuhashi, Keisuke Fujii, And Masaru Hongo
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Mitsuhashi, Keisuke Fujii, and Masaru Hongo

We investigate the low-energy dynamics of small-amplitude surface oscillations of spherical superfluid droplets in vacuum. Starting from the effective field theory of superfluid phonons, we derive an effective action governing the surface oscillations under a fixed particle-number constraint. The no…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an effective field theory for surface oscillations of superfluid droplets, focusing on low-energy dynamics under fixed particle number.
motivation: To understand the low-energy dynamics of surface oscillations in self-bound superfluid droplets, which are relevant for atomic and molecular physics.
method: Starting from an effective field theory of superfluid phonons, the authors derive an effective action for surface oscillations with a fixed particle-number constraint.
result: An effective action governing small-amplitude surface oscillations is obtained, capturing the low-energy dynamics.
conclusion: The effective theory provides a framework for studying surface oscillations in superfluid droplets, with potential applications in ultracold atomic systems.

title: Vortex Dynamics In Rotating Dipolar Supersolids Across Josephson And Self-trapping Regimes
authors: Aitor Alaña, Michele Modugno, And Pablo Capuzzi
abstract:
Author(s): Aitor Alaña, Michele Modugno, and Pablo Capuzzi

We investigate vortex nucleation and transport in a rotating dipolar supersolid arranged in a triangular droplet lattice, exploiting its description as an array of weakly linked condensates. By considering both Josephson and macroscopic self-trapping dynamics, we show that local phase differences be…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vortex dynamics in rotating dipolar supersolids, focusing on Josephson and self-trapping regimes in a triangular droplet lattice.
motivation: Understanding vortex nucleation and transport in supersolids is important for characterizing these exotic quantum phases.
method: The authors model the supersolid as an array of weakly linked condensates and analyze phase differences to study vortex dynamics.
result: They find that local phase differences lead to distinct vortex behaviors depending on Josephson or self-trapping dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into vortex phenomena in supersolids but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Atom Beam Splitter With Internal State Selection Using Spin-dependent Optical Standing Wave Potentials
authors: Igor Kuzmenko, Yshai Avishai, And Y. B. Band
abstract:
Author(s): Igor Kuzmenko, Yshai Avishai, and Y. B. Band

We propose an atom beam splitter that enables the manipulation of the internal spin state of the atoms in the output beams using a spin-dependent optical potential. The utility of such an atom beam splitter is demonstrated theoretically through its application in measuring the Aharonov-Casher phase …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013306] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom beam splitter using spin-dependent optical potentials to measure the Aharonov-Casher phase.
motivation: To enable manipulation of internal spin states in atom interferometry for phase measurements.
method: Theoretical proposal using spin-dependent optical standing wave potentials to split and select atomic spin states.
result: Demonstrates the utility for measuring the Aharonov-Casher phase.
conclusion: The proposed beam splitter can be used for precision measurements of geometric phases.

title: Optical Coprocessor Based On Spontaneous Brillouin Scattering
authors: I. V. Vovchenko, A. A. Zyablovsky, A. A. Pukhov, And E. S. Andrianov
abstract:
Author(s): I. V. Vovchenko, A. A. Zyablovsky, A. A. Pukhov, and E. S. Andrianov

Analog coprocessors for neural networks are an intensively developing field. They provide approximate results of computations for relatively low energy cost and at high speed. We show that a set of ring resonators with Brillouin interaction between photons and phonons, being coupled to a waveguide, …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013501] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optical coprocessor using Brillouin scattering in ring resonators for analog neural network computation.
motivation: Analog coprocessors can provide fast, energy-efficient approximate computations for neural networks, but current implementations face challenges in scalability and performance.
method: The authors design a set of ring resonators with Brillouin interaction between photons and phonons, coupled to a waveguide, to perform matrix-vector multiplications.
result: They demonstrate that the system can implement linear operations with high fidelity and low power consumption, suitable for neural network acceleration.
conclusion: The Brillouin-based optical coprocessor offers a promising platform for analog computing, though further development is needed for practical integration.

title: Temporal Parity-time Phase Transition In Photonic Time-modulated Media
authors: Rui-Chuan Zhang, Shu Yang, Yixin Sha, Zetao Xie, And Yi Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui-Chuan Zhang, Shu Yang, Yixin Sha, Zetao Xie, and Yi Yang

Temporal modulation of photonic media generally induces effective gain and loss and thus non-Hermitian wave dynamics. Here, we show that under a temporally [MATH]-symmetric modulation, such media can nevertheless exhibit Hermiticity and a temporal [MATH] phase transition. We prove th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies temporal parity-time phase transitions in photonic time-modulated media, focusing on non-Hermitian wave dynamics and Hermiticity restoration under symmetric modulation.
motivation: To understand how temporal modulation of photonic media can induce effective gain and loss, and to explore the possibility of Hermiticity and phase transitions in such non-Hermitian systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic medium under temporally PT-symmetric modulation, deriving conditions for Hermiticity and characterizing the temporal PT phase transition.
result: They prove that under certain temporal modulation, the system can exhibit Hermiticity and a temporal PT phase transition, with implications for wave dynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals a temporal analog of PT symmetry in photonic systems, offering insights into non-Hermitian physics but with limited direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Enhancement And Reentrant Topological Transitions In A Mosaic Trimer Lattice
authors: Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, and Shu Chen

We study the topological properties of a one-dimensional quasiperiodic-potential-modulated mosaic trimer lattice. To begin with, we first investigate the topological properties of the model in the clean limit free of quasiperiodic modulation based on analytical derivations and numerical calculations…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014204] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic mosaic trimer lattice, focusing on topological enhancement and reentrant transitions.
motivation: To understand topological properties in quasiperiodic systems and explore novel topological transitions beyond conventional periodic lattices.
method: Analytical derivations and numerical calculations are used to characterize the topological invariants and phase diagram of the mosaic trimer lattice with quasiperiodic modulation.
result: The system exhibits topological enhancement and reentrant topological transitions as the quasiperiodic potential strength varies.
conclusion: The findings reveal rich topological behavior in quasiperiodic systems, contributing to the understanding of topological phases in disordered lattices.

title: Long-range Spin Glass In A Field At Zero Temperature
authors: Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, And Tommaso Rizzo
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, and Tommaso Rizzo

We compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field on a one-dimensional long-range model, a proxy for higher-dimensional systems. Our approach is based on a novel loop expansion within the Bethe [MATH]-layer formalism, whose adaptation to this specific case is de…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field using a long-range one-dimensional model and a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism.
motivation: Understanding spin glass transitions in a field is a challenging problem in condensed matter physics; the authors aim to provide accurate critical exponents using a novel analytical method.
method: They develop a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism adapted to the long-range model, which serves as a proxy for higher-dimensional systems.
result: They compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field.
conclusion: The approach yields precise exponents and demonstrates the utility of the Bethe-layer formalism for such transitions.

title: Real-time Detection Of Critical Slowing Down In Ultrafast Quenches Of Superconductivity
authors: Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, And Chiara Ciccarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, and Chiara Ciccarelli

We employ optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy to chart the ultrafast superconductivity suppression in NbN over a broad range of excitation fluences. Our measurements uncover a pronounced lengthening of the superconductivity quenching time when the absorbed optical energy is close to the condensation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies ultrafast suppression of superconductivity in NbN using optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy, focusing on critical slowing down near the condensation energy threshold.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of superconductivity suppression under ultrafast optical excitation is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast electronics.
method: Optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy is used to measure the superconductivity quenching time as a function of absorbed optical energy in NbN thin films.
result: A pronounced lengthening of the quenching time is observed when the absorbed energy approaches the condensation energy, indicating critical slowing down.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the non-equilibrium dynamics of superconductors and the nature of the phase transition under ultrafast excitation.

title: Majorana Signatures In Planar Tunneling Through A Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, And Natalia B. Perkins
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, and Natalia B. Perkins

We propose a planar tunneling setup to probe vacancy-bound Majorana modes in the chiral Kitaev spin liquid. In this geometry, the inelastic tunneling conductance can be expressed directly in terms of real-space spin correlations, establishing a link between measurable spectra and the underlying frac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Majorana signatures in planar tunneling through a Kitaev spin liquid, focusing on vacancy-bound Majorana modes and their detection via spin correlations.
motivation: To propose a planar tunneling setup that can probe Majorana modes in chiral Kitaev spin liquids, linking measurable conductance to fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors derive an expression for inelastic tunneling conductance in terms of real-space spin correlations, using a planar geometry to enhance sensitivity to vacancy-bound Majorana modes.
result: The tunneling conductance spectra show distinct signatures of Majorana modes bound to vacancies, providing a direct link between experimental observables and the underlying fractionalized excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup offers a feasible experimental approach to detect Majorana modes in Kitaev spin liquids, advancing the study of topological quantum matter.

title: Magnetic Skyrmion Lattice Disclinations In Pentagon- And Heptagon-shaped FeGe Nanostructures
authors: Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, And Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, and Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski

Magnetic skyrmions typically form hexagonal lattices in chiral magnets, where translational defects such as dislocations are well known but angular defects remain largely unexplored. Here, the authors stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped FeGe nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam milling. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography reveal their magnetic and elastic structure. Supported by micromagnetic simulations, the results show how geometric confinement engineers defects in skyrmion lattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024411] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological defects (disclinations) in magnetic skyrmion lattices confined to pentagon- and heptagon-shaped nanostructures.
motivation: Understanding and controlling defects in skyrmion lattices is important for spintronic applications, but angular defects like disclinations have been largely unexplored.
method: The authors fabricate FeGe nanostructures with pentagon and heptagon shapes using focused ion beam milling, and characterize the magnetic structure using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography, supported by micromagnetic simulations.
result: They stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations and reveal their magnetic and elastic structure.
conclusion: Geometric confinement can engineer defects in skyrmion lattices, providing a route to control topological textures in nanoscale magnets.

title: Interaction-driven Quantum Criticality In Two-dimensional Quadratic Band Crossing Semimetals With Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yi-Kun Fang And Jing Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Kun Fang and Jing Wang

We present a systematic investigation of all 16 marginally relevant fermion-fermion interactions in two-dimensional (2D) time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals hosting a quadratic band crossing point (QBCP). Employing a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach that treats every inter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034102] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven quantum criticality in 2D time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals with a quadratic band crossing point.
motivation: Understanding the effects of fermion-fermion interactions in semimetals with quadratic band crossings is important for exploring novel quantum phases.
method: The authors use a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach to analyze all 16 marginally relevant interactions.
result: They identify the quantum critical behavior and possible instabilities driven by these interactions.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of interacting topological semimetals but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Higher-order Topological type-II Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, And Zhen Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, and Zhen Gao

Recently, higher-order topological phases have been extended from Euclidean lattices to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices. Though higher-order topological type-I hyperbolic lattices have been extensively studied, their counterpart, higher-order topological type-II hyperbolic lattices, have never yet…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological phases in hyperbolic lattices, specifically type-II hyperbolic lattices.
motivation: Higher-order topological phases have been extended to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices, but type-II hyperbolic lattices have not been explored.
method: The authors construct type-II hyperbolic lattices and analyze their topological properties using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate the existence of higher-order topological states in type-II hyperbolic lattices.
conclusion: This work extends the understanding of topological phases to a new class of hyperbolic lattices.

title: Observing Complementary Lucas Sequences Using non-Hermitian Zero Modes
authors: Li Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Li Ge

The Lucas sequences are integers defined by a homogeneous recurrence relation. They include the well-known Fibonacci numbers, which appear abundantly in nature. The complementary Lucas numbers, defined by the same recurrence relation, are less well-known. In this work, we show that such complementar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that complementary Lucas sequences can be observed using non-Hermitian zero modes in a photonic system.
motivation: To demonstrate that mathematical sequences like Lucas numbers can be physically realized in non-Hermitian systems, bridging number theory and photonics.
method: The authors design a photonic lattice with non-Hermitian zero modes whose eigenvalues follow complementary Lucas sequences, and analyze the recurrence relations.
result: They observe the complementary Lucas numbers in the energy spectrum of the non-Hermitian system.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian zero modes provide a platform to observe integer sequences, revealing a connection between number theory and non-Hermitian physics.

title: Dominant Superconductivity In A Three-component Hubbard Chain
authors: Sheng Chen, Qiao Yang, Wéi Wú, And Fadi Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Chen, Qiao Yang, Wéi Wú, and Fadi Sun

Understanding superconductivity emerging from repulsive fermions remains a major challenge in condensed matter physics. In this paper, we investigate the pairing tendencies in a one-dimensional, three-component repulsive Hubbard model, using the density matrix renormalization group method. At half f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045105] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity in a three-component Hubbard chain using DMRG, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconductivity from repulsive fermions is a key challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method to investigate pairing tendencies in a one-dimensional three-component repulsive Hubbard model.
result: The paper identifies dominant superconducting pairing correlations in the model.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of superconductivity in multi-component fermionic systems.

title: Correlation-driven Metallic Phase Revealed By An Extended Two-orbital Coherent Potential Approximation
authors: Xiu-Cai Jiang, Jin-Rong Xu, And Yu-Zhong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiu-Cai Jiang, Jin-Rong Xu, and Yu-Zhong Zhang

The extension of single-site coherent potential approximation (CPA) to multiorbital Hubbard models with full Hund's coupling has remained challenging due to the difficulty of constructing an appropriate alloy-analogy model. Here, we decompose the exact Green's functions of the atomic-limit two-orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the coherent potential approximation to multiorbital Hubbard models with Hund's coupling to study correlation-driven metallic phases.
motivation: Extending single-site CPA to multiorbital Hubbard models with full Hund's coupling has been challenging due to the difficulty of constructing an appropriate alloy-analogy model.
method: The authors decompose the exact Green's functions of the atomic-limit two-orbital model and develop an extended CPA that incorporates Hund's coupling.
result: The method reveals a correlation-driven metallic phase not captured by standard single-site approximations.
conclusion: The extended CPA provides a more accurate description of correlated electron systems with orbital and spin degrees of freedom.

title: Broken Su(3) Flavor Symmetry In A Quantum Hall Valley Nematic
authors: G. Krizman, A. Kazakov, C.-W. Cho, V. V. Volobuev, A. Majou, E. Ben Achour, T. Wojtowicz, G. Bauer, Y. Guldner, B. A. Piot, Th. Jolicoeur, G. Springholz, And L.-A. de Vaulchier
abstract:
Author(s): G. Krizman, A. Kazakov, C.-W. Cho, V. V. Volobuev, A. Majou, E. Ben Achour, T. Wojtowicz, G. Bauer, Y. Guldner, B. A. Piot, Th. Jolicoeur, G. Springholz, and L.-A. de Vaulchier

Under high magnetic fields, electrons can organize and break internal symmetries associated with their pseudospin. Here, the authors demonstrate broken SU(3) symmetry assigned to the valley degree of freedom in the Pb(Sn)Se system by following the valley population revealed by the integer quantum Hall effect. A tilted magnetic field acts as a Zeeman valley field, lifting the valley pseudospin degeneracy and driving valley nematic order.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045109] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of broken SU(3) valley symmetry in Pb(Sn)Se quantum Hall systems under high magnetic fields.
motivation: To investigate internal symmetry breaking in quantum Hall systems, specifically the valley degree of freedom in Pb(Sn)Se.
method: Magnetotransport measurements in tilted magnetic fields to lift valley degeneracy and observe valley nematic order.
result: Demonstrated broken SU(3) symmetry associated with valley pseudospin, revealed by integer quantum Hall effect.
conclusion: The findings show valley nematic order driven by Zeeman-like valley field, contributing to understanding of symmetry breaking in quantum Hall systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Transverse Currents In Rashba Metal Junctions Under Out-of-plane Zeeman Fields
authors: Megha Bera, Bijay Kumar Sahoo, And Abhiram Soori
abstract:
Author(s): Megha Bera, Bijay Kumar Sahoo, and Abhiram Soori

We study charge transport across a junction between a normal metal and a Rashba metal in the presence of a Zeeman field applied to the spin-orbit coupled region. While an out-of-plane Zeeman field does not generate a transverse response in a homogeneous Rashba system, we show that such a junction ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045302] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal transverse currents in Rashba metal junctions under out-of-plane Zeeman fields, a condensed matter transport phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding charge transport in spin-orbit coupled systems with Zeeman fields is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a normal metal-Rashba metal junction using scattering formalism and calculate transverse currents.
result: They find that a junction can generate nonreciprocal transverse currents even with an out-of-plane Zeeman field, which would not occur in a homogeneous system.
conclusion: The junction geometry enables new transport effects, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Prediction Of The Hubbard $u$ Parameter From Scanning Tunneling Microscopy Images Of Moiré Systems Using Image Recognition
authors: Nachiket Tanksale And Tobias Stauber
abstract:
Author(s): Nachiket Tanksale and Tobias Stauber

The atomistic Hubbard interaction [MATH], representing the on-site Coulomb repulsion, serves as a pivotal parameter in theoretical models describing correlated systems, yet its precise experimental determination, especially in moiré systems, remains challenging. Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) prov…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to predict the Hubbard U parameter from STM images of moiré systems.
motivation: Determining the Hubbard U parameter experimentally is challenging, especially in moiré systems; the authors aim to provide a method to extract it from STM images.
method: They employ image recognition techniques (machine learning) on simulated STM images of moiré systems to predict the on-site Coulomb repulsion U.
result: The method successfully predicts U from STM images, offering a new way to estimate this parameter.
conclusion: Machine learning can be used to extract key interaction parameters from experimental images, aiding the study of correlated systems.

title: Fractionalized Superconductivity And Spin Stiffnesses In The Su(2) Gauge Theory Of The Two-dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Demetrio Vilardi And Pietro M. Bonetti
abstract:
Author(s): Demetrio Vilardi and Pietro M. Bonetti

We consider the SU(2) gauge theory for spin fluctuations in the two-dimensional Hubbard model, where the electron field is fractionalized in terms of spinons and chargons. In this theory, spinons are described by a nonlinear sigma model, while chargons are treated as fermions at a mean-field level. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fractionalized superconductivity in the 2D Hubbard model using an SU(2) gauge theory, focusing on spin stiffnesses and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between spin fluctuations and superconductivity in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in the context of high-Tc superconductors.
method: The authors employ an SU(2) gauge theory where electrons are fractionalized into spinons (described by a nonlinear sigma model) and chargons (treated at mean-field level), and compute spin stiffnesses to characterize superconducting phases.
result: The analysis reveals distinct spin stiffness behaviors associated with different superconducting phases, providing insights into the nature of fractionalized superconductivity.
conclusion: The SU(2) gauge theory captures key features of spin fluctuations and superconductivity in the Hubbard model, but the results are primarily relevant to condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Cavity-assisted Spin Selection In One-dimensional Conductors
authors: Vivek Kumar, Joshua Coop, Yingshi Duo, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, And Sanjeev Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Vivek Kumar, Joshua Coop, Yingshi Duo, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, and Sanjeev Kumar

Spontaneous spin polarization in quasi-one-dimensional (1D) electron systems is inherently fragile, often masked by structural disorder or potential anharmonicity. Here we report the deterministic stabilization of an exchange-driven spin gap, manifesting as a robust [MATH] conductance pla…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.

Author(s): F. Ţolea and M. Ţolea

We consider random sequential adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares and derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function [MATH], the fraction of positions accessible to an additional square, up to fourth order in the coverage [MATH]. At low coverage, the reduction of available space can be …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014110] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the low-density expansion of the availability function in random sequential adsorption of aligned squares, a problem in statistical physics.
motivation: Understanding the kinetics of irreversible deposition processes is important for modeling physical phenomena such as protein adsorption or particle deposition.
method: The authors derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function up to fourth order in coverage using combinatorial and geometric arguments.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the coefficients of the expansion, showing how the available area decreases with coverage.
conclusion: The work provides a precise analytical result for a specific RSA model, contributing to the theory of random sequential adsorption.

title: Persistent Imbalance In Open Networks With Coevolutionary Dynamics
authors: S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, And G. Reza Jafari
abstract:
Author(s): S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, and G. Reza Jafari

Societies are quintessential open systems, shaped by internal dynamics as well as external influences. The question is how these external influences alter the collective behavior and network dynamics. To answer this, we investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coevolutionary balance dynamics in open networks, focusing on societal systems and external influences.
motivation: Understanding how external influences alter collective behavior and network dynamics in open systems like societies.
method: Investigates coevolutionary dynamics in a system of independent and open networks using a balance theory approach.
result: Finds persistent imbalance in open networks with coevolutionary dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into how external influences shape network dynamics and collective behavior in open systems.

title: Ising Phase Transitions In Networks With Tunable Degree-degree Correlations
authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of Ising model phase transitions on networks with tunable degree-degree correlations.
motivation: To understand how degree-degree correlations affect critical phenomena in complex networks.
method: Construct networks with truncated power-law degree distribution and apply Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring to tune correlations; simulate ferromagnetic Ising model via Monte Carlo.
result: Phase transition properties depend on correlation strength and network structure.
conclusion: Degree-degree correlations significantly influence Ising model phase transitions in complex networks.

title: Unveiling The Impact Of Cross-order Hyperdegree Correlations In Contagion Processes On Hypergraphs
authors: Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Andrés Guzmán, Federico Malizia, and István Z. Kiss

Contagion processes in social systems often involve interactions that go beyond pairwise contacts. Higher-order networks, represented as hypergraphs, have been widely used to model multibody interactions, and their presence can drastically alter contagion dynamics compared to traditional network mod…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies contagion processes on hypergraphs, focusing on the impact of cross-order hyperdegree correlations.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions affect epidemic spreading is important for modeling social systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model for contagion on hypergraphs and analyze the role of correlations between hyperdegrees of different orders.
result: They find that cross-order correlations can significantly alter the epidemic threshold and outbreak size.
conclusion: The work contributes to network science and epidemiology, but is unrelated to the specified research interests.

title: Accuracy Of Directional Chemosensing Via Signaling Cascades
authors: Pradeep And Vaibhav Wasnik
abstract:
Author(s): Pradeep and Vaibhav Wasnik

Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, raising fundamental questions about the limits of sensing. While receptor-level constraints in chemosensing are well characterized, the role of intracellular signaling remains underexplored. We develop a theoretical framework combi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for directional chemosensing via signaling cascades, focusing on accuracy limits in biochemical sensing.
motivation: Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, but the role of intracellular signaling in sensing accuracy is underexplored.
method: The authors combine a stochastic model of receptor-ligand binding with a signaling cascade to compute the accuracy of directional sensing.
result: They find that signaling cascades can enhance sensing accuracy beyond receptor-level limits under certain conditions.
conclusion: Intracellular signaling plays a crucial role in determining the fundamental limits of chemosensing accuracy.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy, which is a topic in classical statistical mechanics and plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids is important for dusty plasma physics, but it does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa fluids are performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The excess entropy identifies a supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamics of classical Yukawa fluids but has no relevance to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Djamel Benredjem And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Djamel Benredjem and Jean-Christophe Pain

The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict plasma opacity under stellar conditions, focusing on iron and nickel.
motivation: Accurate opacity predictions are crucial for understanding stellar interiors and spectra, but calculations under nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive.
method: The authors employ a deep learning model trained on existing opacity data to predict spectral opacities for iron and nickel plasmas.
result: The deep learning approach achieves fast and accurate opacity predictions, matching theoretical calculations.
conclusion: Deep learning can serve as an efficient surrogate for opacity calculations in astrophysical plasmas.

title: From Geometry To Strategy: Symmetry Breaking In Cooperative Multiagent Active Dynamics
authors: Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, And Sergey Savel'ev
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, and Sergey Savel'ev

We investigate the emergence of cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems, where autonomous agents, modeled as active particles, learn to capture targets dynamically regenerated in geometrically distinct arenas. Using proximal policy optimization, we study ci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems using active particles, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how autonomous agents learn to capture targets in geometrically distinct arenas, exploring emergent strategies.
method: They use proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train agents modeled as active particles in a multiagent reinforcement learning framework.
result: The study reveals symmetry breaking and emergent cooperative/competitive behaviors depending on arena geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into multiagent active dynamics but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Higher-order Adaptive Behaviors Outperform Pairwise Strategies In Mitigating Contagion Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, And Alain Barrat
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, and Alain Barrat

When exposed to a contagion phenomenon, individuals may respond to the perceived risk of infection by adopting behavioral changes, aiming to reduce their exposure or their risk of infecting others. The social cost of such adaptive behaviors and their impact on the contagion dynamics have been invest…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order adaptive behaviors (e.g., group-level responses) outperform pairwise strategies in mitigating contagion dynamics on networks.
motivation: Understanding how individuals adapt their behavior in response to contagion is crucial for designing effective mitigation strategies, but most models only consider pairwise interactions.
method: The authors develop a model of contagion with adaptive behaviors at both pairwise and higher-order (group) levels, and analyze the dynamics using numerical simulations and analytical approximations.
result: Higher-order adaptive behaviors are more effective at reducing the final epidemic size and delaying the peak of infection compared to pairwise strategies alone.
conclusion: Incorporating group-level behavioral responses can significantly improve contagion mitigation, highlighting the importance of higher-order interactions in epidemic modeling.

title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Sampling To Model Lagrangian Tracer Dispersion In Turbulent Boundary Layer
authors: Fabian Schindler And Jörg Schumacher
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Schindler and Jörg Schumacher

We present a quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QE-MCMC) method to sample turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution that depends on all three components and height to model the transport and dispersion of massless Lagrangian tracer particles in two different turbulent s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033031] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layers.
motivation: Turbulent dispersion of particles is important for environmental and engineering applications, but classical MCMC can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors propose a quantum-enhanced MCMC algorithm that uses quantum sampling to accelerate the generation of turbulent acceleration vectors from a joint target distribution.
result: The quantum-enhanced method shows improved sampling efficiency compared to classical MCMC for the specific turbulent flow scenarios considered.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced MCMC can be a useful tool for computational fluid dynamics, though practical quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated on larger scales.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biophysics and soft matter, but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze phase separation near a surface under finite molecule number constraints.
result: They find that surface phase separation is significantly altered by confinement, with implications for cellular organization.
conclusion: Surface effects are crucial for understanding phase separation in cells, but the work is unrelated to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Noiseless Limit And Improved-prior Limit Of The Maximum Entropy Method And Their Implications For The Analytic Continuation Problem
authors: Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, And Tobias Dornheim
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Chuna, Nicholas Barnfield, Paul Hamann, Sebastian Schwalbe, Michael P. Friedlander, and Tobias Dornheim

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are uniquely capable of providing exact simulations of quantum many-body systems. Unfortunately, the applications of a QMC simulation are limited because extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem. Across the many fields that us…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033009] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the maximum entropy method for analytic continuation in quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on its noiseless and improved-prior limits.
motivation: Quantum Monte Carlo methods provide exact simulations of quantum many-body systems but extracting dynamic properties requires solving the analytic continuation problem, which is ill-posed.
method: The authors derive the noiseless limit and improved-prior limit of the maximum entropy method, providing analytical insights into its behavior.
result: They show that in the noiseless limit, the method recovers the exact spectral function, and with an improved prior, the reconstruction quality is enhanced.
conclusion: The findings offer guidance for applying the maximum entropy method to analytic continuation, improving reliability in extracting dynamic properties from QMC data.

title: Markov Inequality As A Tool For Linear-scaling Estimation Of Local Observables
authors: H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Veiga, D. R. Pinheiro, J. P. Santos Pires, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

We introduce a linear-scaling stochastic method to compute real-space maps of any positive local spectral operator in a tight-binding model. By employing positive semidefinite estimators, the sampling error at each site can be rigorously bounded relative to the mean via the Markov inequality, overco…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033015] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A linear-scaling stochastic method for computing local spectral observables in tight-binding models using Markov inequality bounds.
motivation: Efficient computation of local observables in large tight-binding models is computationally expensive; a linear-scaling method is needed.
method: Uses positive semidefinite estimators and Markov inequality to bound sampling error, enabling linear-scaling estimation of local spectral operators.
result: The method achieves linear scaling with system size and provides rigorous error bounds, demonstrated on graphene nanoribbons.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical tool for studying local properties in large quantum systems, but is primarily a computational technique without deep information-theoretic or thermodynamic insights.

title: Arbitrary Control Of non-Hermitian Skin Modes Via Disorder And An Electric Field
authors: Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, And Franco Nori
abstract:
Author(s): Zhao-Fan Cai, Yang Li, Yu-Ran Zhang, Xiaomin Wei, Zhongmin Yang, Tao Liu, and Franco Nori

The non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), characterized by the accumulation of a macroscopic number of bulk states at system boundaries, is a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics. However, in higher dimensions, achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate remains a major challenge. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033021] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the control of non-Hermitian skin modes using disorder and electric fields, focusing on non-Hermitian physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Achieving deterministic control over where skin modes accumulate in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems is a major challenge.
method: The authors propose using disorder and electric fields to arbitrarily control the localization of non-Hermitian skin modes.
result: They demonstrate that disorder and electric fields can effectively manipulate skin mode accumulation, enabling flexible control.
conclusion: This work provides a method for controlling non-Hermitian skin effects, which may have applications in non-Hermitian physics but is not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Engineering Magnetotransport Through Hierarchical Symmetry In Weyl Semimetal Superlattices
authors: Nathan C. Drucker, Federico Balduini, Jules Schadt, Lorenzo Rocchino, Tathagata Paul, Vicky Hasse, Claudia Felser, Heinz Schmid, Cezar B. Zota, And Bernd Gotsmann
abstract:

Superlattice engineering, the introduction of periodic potentials to a material, can induce selective scattering events that modify the electrical properties of the material in predictable ways. Extending superlattice engineering to three-dimensional (3D) electronic materials can expand the tunabili…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033023] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetotransport in Weyl semimetal superlattices, focusing on symmetry-induced scattering and electrical properties.
motivation: To explore how periodic potentials in 3D materials can tune electrical properties via selective scattering.
method: The authors engineer superlattices in Weyl semimetals and measure magnetotransport to characterize the effect of hierarchical symmetry.
result: They demonstrate controllable modification of magnetotransport through superlattice engineering.
conclusion: Superlattice engineering is a viable method for tuning transport in topological semimetals.

title: Adversarial Vulnerability Of Machine-learning Surrogates For Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, And Jun-Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jian-Nan Chen, Xiao-Yan Cao, and Jun-Jie Zhang

Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet their robustness to small, structured input perturbations remains insufficiently characterized. Conventional adversarial training is largely impractical for artificial intelligence for CFD (AI4CFD…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial vulnerability of machine-learning surrogates for computational fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Machine-learning surrogates are used to accelerate CFD, but their robustness to small input perturbations is not well characterized.
method: The authors analyze adversarial attacks on neural network surrogates for CFD and evaluate their impact on prediction accuracy.
result: The surrogates are found to be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, which can cause significant errors in predicted flow fields.
conclusion: Adversarial robustness must be considered when deploying ML surrogates in CFD applications.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: Demonstrates the algorithm on a one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, showing accurate excitation energies.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach can efficiently compute quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films
authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

Electron-phonon interactions play a central role in determining charge and heat transport in condensed matter systems, but in disordered and low-dimensional materials, this coupling can be strongly suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport phenomena. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023360] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron-phonon interactions and current bistability in disordered insulating films, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding charge and heat transport in disordered materials where electron-phonon coupling is suppressed.
method: Extended hot-electron model and experimental measurements on amorphous YxSi1-x films.
result: Observation of current bistability and analysis of electron-phonon coupling effects.
conclusion: The model explains nontrivial transport phenomena in disordered insulators.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia

Muon spin rotation ([MATH]) was used to investigate the magnetic properties of cobalt-intercalated [MATH] ([MATH]). [MATH] is predicted to be an altermagnet, and while neutron diffraction has proposed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: To provide local probe evidence supporting the predicted altermagnetic state in Co1/4NbSe2, which has been proposed by neutron diffraction.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on single crystals of Co1/4NbSe2 to probe the internal magnetic fields.
result: The μSR data reveal signatures consistent with altermagnetism, supporting the earlier neutron diffraction findings.
conclusion: The study confirms the altermagnetic nature of Co1/4NbSe2 using a local probe, adding to the understanding of this novel magnetic phase.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, and Carsten Timm

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2, focusing on its locally noncentrosymmetric crystal structure.
motivation: Locally noncentrosymmetric materials exhibit unique phenomena due to sublattice degrees of freedom, and CeRh2As2 is a compelling example that may host novel superconducting phases.
method: The authors use a theoretical model based on the electronic structure of CeRh2As2 to analyze possible superconducting order parameters and their interplay with magnetic ordering.
result: They identify composite superconducting orders that mix spin-singlet and spin-triplet components, and show how these orders compete or coexist with magnetism.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding the unusual superconducting properties of CeRh2As2 and guide future experiments.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Phase-space Methods For Near-resonant Light Propagation
authors: Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, and Gerd Leuchs

We study the dynamics of light interacting with a near-resonant atomic medium using the truncated Wigner and positive [MATH] phase-space representations. By mapping the atomic degrees of freedom via the Jordan-Schwinger transformation, we first analyze the system under unitary evolution before extendin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023353] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks phase-space methods for simulating near-resonant light propagation through atomic media.
motivation: To evaluate the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares phase-space simulations with exact solutions for unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: Identifies regimes where each method performs well and where they break down, providing guidelines for choosing the appropriate representation.
conclusion: Phase-space methods are useful for certain parameter regimes but have limitations; careful benchmarking is needed for reliable simulations.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis
