title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning tunneling microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field and enhance fluorescence.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding 2D magnetism and its potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified framework is lacking.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to treat these systems.
result: They show how these methods unify diverse approaches and provide tools for analyzing such systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key developments and future opportunities in spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological characteristics of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with ongoing experimental and theoretical developments, offering insights into frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in quantum systems, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of existing theoretical methods and an outlook on their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need to be better integrated into applied fields like photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion dynamics and interactions, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the standard model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson couplings and discusses the implications for fundamental symmetries and dark matter candidates.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with many open questions; future experiments may further constrain or discover such interactions.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields, analyzing which assumptions of the classical bounds are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, linearity, or homogeneity.
conclusion: Understanding these violations allows the development of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits, but the findings are primarily in materials science and classical thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a promising avenue for studying fundamental physics, but remains largely exploratory and not directly tied to the user's core interests.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify and understand the role of self-alignment in active systems, which leads to novel phenomena.
method: Review of existing models and experiments, presenting a unified mathematical framework.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors like orbiting and synchronized motion, with applications in biology and robotics.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter, offering a new perspective for future research.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity at the quantum level.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence, collapse models, and entanglement generation, along with experimental platforms such as matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics.
result: Current experiments are testing whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement between massive particles, with results guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems provide a promising avenue to explore the interface of quantum mechanics and gravity, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Tailoring Pure Valley-Zeeman Spin-Orbit Coupling In ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$-Encapsulated Monolayer Graphene
authors: Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, And Geliang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, and Geliang Yu

Clearly resolved Landau levels reveal a symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering driven by competition between fixed valley–Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley-Zeeman spin-orbit coupling in WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene, focusing on Landau level reordering.
motivation: To understand the interplay between valley-Zeeman splitting and cyclotron energy in graphene heterostructures.
method: Magneto-transport measurements on WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene devices.
result: Observation of symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering due to competition between fixed valley-Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.
conclusion: The results demonstrate tunable spin-orbit coupling in graphene, relevant for spintronics and valleytronics.

title: Microwave Vortex Beam Lasing Via Photonic Time Crystals
authors: Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Microwave lasing carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) holds significant potential for advanced applications in fields such as high-capacity communications, precision sensing, and radar imaging. However, conventional approaches to masers fail to produce emission with embedded OAM. The recent emerg…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates microwave lasing with orbital angular momentum using photonic time crystals.
motivation: Conventional masers cannot produce emission with embedded OAM; photonic time crystals offer a new mechanism to generate vortex beams.
method: The authors propose and analyze a photonic time crystal structure that supports OAM-carrying modes and achieves lasing through temporal modulation.
result: They show that microwave vortex beams can be generated with controlled OAM states, enabling potential applications in communications and sensing.
conclusion: Photonic time crystals provide a viable platform for OAM lasing, expanding capabilities in microwave photonics.

title: Three-Dimensional Wide-Bandwidth Quantum Energy Truncation Terahertz Coherence Tomography
authors: Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, And Andreas Mandelis
abstract:
Author(s): Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, and Andreas Mandelis

We report a quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography technique that enables highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses. The method exploits resonant photon loss when the emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta. Reflected THz radiation is rec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026901] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A terahertz imaging technique using quantum energy truncation for molecular-specific tomography.
motivation: To achieve highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses for imaging applications.
method: Exploits resonant photon loss when emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta, and uses reflected THz radiation.
result: Demonstrates three-dimensional wide-bandwidth quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography.
conclusion: The technique enables molecular-specific THz imaging with potential applications in materials characterization.

title: Revising The Superexchange Model For The Planar Iridate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$: From An Analytical Approach To $ab Initio$ Quantum-chemical Computations
authors: L. Siurakshina
abstract:
Author(s): L. Siurakshina

A modified spin-orbital superexchange theory is developed to derive the effective spin Hamiltonian [MATH] governing the exchange interactions between pseudospins-[MATH] on a square lattice, as occurs, for instance, in planar iridium oxide [MATH]. The proced…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024412] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a modified spin-orbital superexchange theory to derive an effective spin Hamiltonian for the planar iridate Ba2IrO4, using analytical methods and ab initio quantum-chemical computations.
motivation: To accurately model the magnetic interactions in Ba2IrO4, which is a candidate material for studying spin-orbit coupling effects and quantum magnetism.
method: The authors develop a modified superexchange theory that includes spin-orbit coupling and use ab initio quantum-chemical computations to parameterize the effective spin Hamiltonian.
result: They derive an effective pseudospin-1/2 Hamiltonian on a square lattice and compute exchange parameters that reproduce experimental observations.
conclusion: The modified superexchange model provides a more accurate description of the magnetic properties of Ba2IrO4, highlighting the importance of spin-orbit coupling in iridates.

title: Origin Of Muon Spin Relaxation And Frequency Shift In Frozen Water Explained By Spin-dipole Quantum Coherences
authors: Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, And Koichiro Shimomura
abstract:
Author(s): Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, and Koichiro Shimomura

To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water with temperature, we performed weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation ([MATH]) measurements over a temperature range of 220 K to 300 K. Using a conventional model with a phenomenological relaxation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034106] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water using spin-dipole quantum coherences, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water across temperatures, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation measurements were performed over 220 K to 300 K, and a model incorporating spin-dipole quantum coherences was used to explain the data.
result: The model successfully reproduces the observed temperature dependence of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift.
conclusion: Spin-dipole quantum coherences are key to understanding muon behavior in water, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Robust Topological Surface States In Skyrmion-host Magnets Eu(Ga,Al)${}_{4}$: Evidence For Dual Topology
authors: Yuki Arai, Kosuke Nakayama, Takemi Kato, Tomonori Nakamura, Asuka Honma, Seigo Souma, Kenichi Ozawa, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Daisuke Shiga, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Yoshinori Okada, Kouji Segawa, And Takafumi Sato
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Arai, Kosuke Nakayama, Takemi Kato, Tomonori Nakamura, Asuka Honma, Seigo Souma, Kenichi Ozawa, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Daisuke Shiga, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Yoshinori Okada, Kouji Segawa, and Takafumi Sato

The interplay between real-space topology such as magnetic skyrmions and momentum-space topology characterized by topological surface states (TSSs) is predicted to realize novel phenomena and functionalities, yet materials hosting both topologies are scarce. Skyrmion-hosting helimagnet family ${\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust topological surface states in skyrmion-host magnets Eu(Ga,Al)4, providing evidence for dual topology.
motivation: The interplay between real-space topology (magnetic skyrmions) and momentum-space topology (topological surface states) is predicted to enable novel phenomena, but materials hosting both are rare.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and first-principles calculations were used to investigate the electronic structure of Eu(Ga,Al)4.
result: Robust topological surface states were observed, confirming the coexistence of skyrmion and topological insulator phases.
conclusion: Eu(Ga,Al)4 is a promising platform for studying dual topology and related functionalities.

title: Tailoring Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy And Anisotropic Magnetocaloric Effect In Ni-doped ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$ Single Crystals
authors: Luozhao Zhang, Liqiang Zeng, Jinbo Yang, Yongfeng Mei, Zhongchong Lin, Zhigao Huang, And Jizhai Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Luozhao Zhang, Liqiang Zeng, Jinbo Yang, Yongfeng Mei, Zhongchong Lin, Zhigao Huang, and Jizhai Cui

The regulation of magnetic anisotropy in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets is critical for enabling spintronic and solid-state cooling applications, yet the microscopic doping mechanism remains poorly understood, as conventional ideal-lattice models fail to reconcile the moderate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014409] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Ni doping on magnetocrystalline anisotropy and the anisotropic magnetocaloric effect in Fe3GaTe2 single crystals.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic anisotropy in 2D van der Waals ferromagnets is important for spintronic and solid-state cooling applications, but the microscopic doping mechanism is poorly understood.
method: The authors synthesize Ni-doped Fe3GaTe2 single crystals and characterize their magnetic properties using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: Ni doping tailors the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and enhances the anisotropic magnetocaloric effect.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into doping strategies for tuning magnetic properties in 2D ferromagnets for potential applications.

title: Intrinsic Structure Of Relaxor Ferroelectrics From First Principles
authors: Xinyu Xu, Kehan Cai, Yubai Shi, Peichen Zhong, And Pinchen Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Xu, Kehan Cai, Yubai Shi, Peichen Zhong, and Pinchen Xie

We introduce FIRE-Swap, a first-principles-based framework for sampling representative compositional structures in complex perovskites using machine-learning interatomic potentials. By combining Monte Carlo chemical swaps with geometric relaxation, the method treats chemical and geometric degrees of…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a first-principles framework for sampling compositional structures in relaxor ferroelectrics using machine-learning interatomic potentials.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics have complex compositional disorder that is difficult to model; the authors aim to efficiently sample representative structures for accurate property prediction.
method: They combine Monte Carlo chemical swaps with geometric relaxation, using a machine-learned interatomic potential to accelerate the sampling.
result: The framework successfully generates realistic structural models that capture the intrinsic disorder of relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The approach enables first-principles-level accuracy for studying relaxor ferroelectrics without exhaustive enumeration of configurations.

title: Coexistence Of Mixed-dimensional Fluctuations And Incommensurate Long-range Order In The Frustrated Antiferromagnet $\mathrm{C}{\mathrm{e}}_{5}\mathrm{Ag}{\mathrm{Pb}}_{3}$
authors: Zhijie Ma, Ying Sun, Jiechen Luo, Sihao Deng, Hongde Wang, Xiuliang Yuan, Kaiqi Zhang, Lunhua He, Cong Wang, And Youguo Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Zhijie Ma, Ying Sun, Jiechen Luo, Sihao Deng, Hongde Wang, Xiuliang Yuan, Kaiqi Zhang, Lunhua He, Cong Wang, and Youguo Shi

Low-dimensional systems host exotic quantum phenomena arising from dimensional confinement and strong electron correlations. Here, we report a prototypical case of site-specific mixed dimensionality in [MATH], which originates from inequivalent Ce1($…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the coexistence of mixed-dimensional fluctuations and incommensurate long-range order in a frustrated antiferromagnet Ce5AgPb3.
motivation: To understand exotic quantum phenomena arising from dimensional confinement and strong electron correlations in low-dimensional systems.
method: Neutron scattering and other experimental techniques were used to study the magnetic structure and fluctuations in Ce5AgPb3.
result: Site-specific mixed dimensionality was observed, with coexisting one-dimensional fluctuations and three-dimensional long-range order.
conclusion: The findings provide a prototypical case of mixed-dimensional magnetism in a frustrated antiferromagnet.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity
authors: Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, And Kunimasa Miyazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, and Kunimasa Miyazaki

Hyperuniformity, the anomalous suppression of density fluctuations in dense particle systems, has been reported in amorphous solids near the jamming transition. This manuscript shows that the value of the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in two dimensions differs from that in three dimensions, unlike previously thought.

#AdvancingField #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hyperuniformity scaling exponents near the jamming transition in bidisperse particle systems, finding a difference between 2D and 3D.
motivation: Hyperuniformity in amorphous solids near jamming is of interest, but the paper focuses on classical soft matter physics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Simulations of bidisperse particle systems near jamming, measuring density fluctuations and scaling exponents.
result: The hyperuniformity scaling exponent differs between two and three dimensions, contrary to previous assumptions of universality.
conclusion: The dimensionality dependence of hyperuniformity near jamming is established, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems. We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator model applied to thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory observations is needed.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory data.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for inferring parameters in thermoacoustic instability models, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, analyzing how spatial embedding affects spreading dynamics.
motivation: Many real temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, but existing activity-driven models ignore spatial aspects. The authors aim to understand how spatial constraints influence dynamical processes on temporal networks.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes are placed in a metric space and connections depend on both activity and spatial distance. They derive analytical expressions for the temporal network's structural properties and simulate spreading processes.
result: The model reveals that spatial embedding can significantly slow down spreading and alter the epidemic threshold compared to the non-spatial activity-driven model. The analytical predictions match simulations well.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal constraints are crucial for accurately modeling spreading processes on real temporal networks, and the proposed model provides a tractable framework for further analysis.

title: Random Motility Regulation As A Generic Mechanism Of Community Formation
authors: Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, and Julien Tailleur

The self-organization of microbial ecosystems involves a large variety of mechanisms, ranging from biochemical signaling to population dynamics. Among these, the role of motility regulation has been little studied, despite the importance of active migration processes. Here we show how weak, random m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random motility regulation leads to community formation in microbial ecosystems, using active matter and population dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the self-organization of microbial ecosystems is important, but the role of motility regulation has been little studied.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating weak, random motility regulation and analyze its effects on community formation.
result: They show that random motility regulation can generically lead to the formation of stable communities.
conclusion: Motility regulation is a generic mechanism for community formation in microbial systems.

title: Locally Resonant Structure Optimal For Creation Of Nonlinear Schrödinger Solitons
authors: Xiezhi Mao And Xinlong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiezhi Mao and Xinlong Wang

A more feasible and flexible approach is developed for emission of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons from an impurity-induced localized wave in the [MATH] model. The impurity structure used for inducing the localized wave is proposed to include an additional elasticity impurity [MATH], as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate nonlinear Schrödinger solitons using a locally resonant impurity structure.
motivation: To develop a more feasible and flexible approach for soliton emission from impurity-induced localized waves.
method: The impurity structure includes an additional elasticity impurity to induce localized waves in the φ^4 model.
result: The approach enables controlled creation of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons.
conclusion: The proposed impurity structure offers a practical way to generate solitons, relevant to nonlinear wave physics.

title: Subexponential Growth Dynamics In Complex Systems: A Piecewise Power-law Model For The Diffusion Of New Words And Names
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hayafumi Watanabe

A study of online language shows that niche terms—like the name of a narrowly popular music group—spread less quickly than mainstream words.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the diffusion of new words and names in online language using a piecewise power-law model, finding that niche terms spread more slowly than mainstream ones.
motivation: Understanding how new words and names spread in complex systems like online language can reveal underlying dynamics of information diffusion.
method: The author proposes a piecewise power-law model to describe subexponential growth dynamics and fits it to empirical data on word and name usage from online sources.
result: The model shows that niche terms exhibit slower diffusion compared to mainstream terms, consistent with subexponential growth patterns.
conclusion: The piecewise power-law model effectively captures the diffusion dynamics of linguistic terms, highlighting differences between niche and mainstream spread.

title: Active Deformation Enhances Target Scanning In Crowded Two-dimensional Self-propelled Particle Simulations
authors: Lucas E. Wiebke And Daniel R. Parisi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas E. Wiebke and Daniel R. Parisi

Self-propelled particles (SPPs) model diverse transport phenomena, including T-cell motility within crowded lymph nodes. Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by T cells remains poorly understood under dense conditions. Here we simulate a two-dimensional system of radius-oscillating …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active deformation in self-propelled particle simulations to enhance target scanning in crowded environments, with applications to T-cell motility.
motivation: Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells by T cells in dense lymph nodes is poorly understood; active deformation may improve scanning efficiency.
method: Two-dimensional simulations of radius-oscillating self-propelled particles are used to model T-cell motility and target scanning.
result: Active deformation enhances target scanning efficiency in crowded conditions compared to non-deforming particles.
conclusion: Active deformation is a beneficial strategy for improving search and scanning in dense active matter systems.

title: Nonclassical Interfacial Response In Ionic Liquids At Blocking Electrodes
authors: Mahdi Yavarian And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Mahdi Yavarian and Roderick Melnik

The linear response of a symmetric binary ionic liquid confined between two parallel, blocking electrodes is analyzed under the influence of electrostatic correlations [MATH] while systematically comparing the effects of two distinct interfacial boundary conditions: the Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev (B…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the linear response of ionic liquids between blocking electrodes, focusing on electrostatic correlations and boundary conditions.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of ionic liquids at interfaces is important for applications in energy storage and electrochemistry.
method: The authors analyze a symmetric binary ionic liquid model using linear response theory and compare two interfacial boundary conditions (Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev and another).
result: They find nonclassical interfacial responses due to electrostatic correlations, with significant differences depending on the boundary condition.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition critically affects the predicted interfacial properties of ionic liquids, which has implications for modeling electrochemical systems.

title: Finite-size Scaling In Quasi-three-dimensional Stick Percolation
authors: Ryan K. Daniels
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan K. Daniels

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations are used to extend universal finite-size scaling from 2D to quasi-3D stick systems with sequential deposition of finite-diameter wires.
result: The paper presents scaling laws and critical exponents for percolation in quasi-3D stick systems.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for finite-size scaling in quasi-3D continuum percolation, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. The coupling strengths coevolve according to a Hebbian adaptation rule and self-organize to support a wide variety of collective states. We observe frequency-clu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration strength.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective dynamical states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Saddle-point Equations In Strong-field Physics With Tailored Fields
authors: Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, And Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, and Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations for above-threshold ionization in strong-field physics.
motivation: Solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides accurate solutions for tailored fields.
conclusion: The PINN approach offers a promising alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, but the work is primarily computational physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, and Ke Lu

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the structural and thermal properties of Schwarz crystals, a type of nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries.
motivation: Schwarz crystals exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability, but the interaction of structural units and thermal transport mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural confinement and thermal transport in Schwarz crystals.
result: They find that the unique nanograin structure and TPMS boundaries lead to suppressed thermal conductivity and enhanced stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design of thermally stable nanostructured materials, but does not directly relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging dynamics of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations are used to model dense ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, varying polymer stiffness.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increasing stiffness leading to slower relaxation and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glassy dynamics of ring polymers but remains within classical polymer physics, without relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. Magnetic multipoles such as octupoles or triakontadipoles have been suggested as potential ferroic order parameters f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a recently discovered phenomenon, and there is a need for quantitative order parameters to characterize it.
method: The authors derive a relation between the spin splitting and magnetic multipoles such as octupoles and triakontadipoles using symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: They show that the spin splitting magnitude is proportional to specific multipole moments, providing a quantitative measure.
conclusion: Higher-order magnetic multipoles serve as effective order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting, enabling systematic classification.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:
Author(s): Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, and Oleg Kogan

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging in a two-dimensional swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects the collective organization and aging behavior in a system of swarmalators, which are coupled oscillators with spatial interactions.
method: The authors extend a previous model of swarmalators with delayed interactions to two dimensions and analyze the resulting crystal structures and aging dynamics.
result: They find that time delay can induce aging in the swarmalator crystal, characterized by a gradual loss of order and eventual melting.
conclusion: Time delay is a key factor in the aging dynamics of active matter systems, with implications for understanding collective behavior in biological and physical systems.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, and Changlin Zheng

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To achieve strong focusing of high-energy electrons using a compact solid-state device.
method: A nanosized pore in solid creates a strong electric field (10 GV/m) via the inner Coulomb potential, acting as an electrostatic lens.
result: The nanopore lens effectively modulates high-energy electrons, demonstrating strong focusing capabilities.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a new approach for electron beam manipulation with potential applications in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: The work aims to explore whether neural networks can be used as cryptographic primitives, specifically collision-resistant hash functions.
method: The authors analyze the computational hardness of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical complexity arguments and algorithmic experiments.
result: They find that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The results are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transition of the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel magnetic phase transition and symmetry breaking in a kagome spin ice system.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall physics and magnetic order control.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale silicon photonic crystals are fabricated and characterized experimentally, with theoretical modeling of radiative loss.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is observed and attributed to radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest the need for loss engineering.

title: Distinct Phenomenon On Chaos Synchrony: Chirality
authors: Gualberto C. Solís-Perales And Ricardo Femat

Among others, chirality is a property of organometallic molecules whose main feature is that the spatial superposition is exclusively observed through a specular plane. A specular plane is a physical kind of subspace onto which chiral objects can already be superposed. That is, chirality corresponds…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chirality in chaos synchrony, a phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To investigate the role of chirality in synchronization of chaotic systems.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of coupled chaotic oscillators with chiral symmetry.
result: Chirality leads to distinct synchronization patterns not observed in achiral systems.
conclusion: Chirality is a relevant property for understanding complex synchronization phenomena.

title: Photoelectron Spectroscopy Of $3s3p$ Doubly Excited Helium Dressed With Strong Near-infrared Laser Fields
authors: Mizuho Fushitani, Chien-Nan Liu, Yuki Ono, Shunsuke Amaike, Wataru Yamazaki, Keiko Kato, Akitaka Matsuda, Shigeki Owada, Makina Yabashi, Yasumasa Hikosaka, Toru Morishita, And Akiyoshi Hishikawa

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013105] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies laser-dressed doubly excited resonances in helium using photoelectron spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand and control correlated two-electron resonances in strong laser fields.
method: Combined experimental photoelectron spectroscopy and theoretical calculations.
result: Established a quantitative approach to characterize short-lived laser-dressed resonances.
conclusion: The method enables control of correlated two-electron resonances in strong fields.

title: Ab Initio Calculations Of The Electronic Structure Of ${\mathrm{Ac}}^{+}$
authors: Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, And Anastasia Borschevsky
abstract:
Author(s): Genevieve Geehan, Marten Luit Reitsma, Johan David Polet, Mustapha Laatiaoui, Julian Berengut, and Anastasia Borschevsky

Accurate spectroscopic investigations of the heaviest elements are inherently challenging, due to their short lifetimes and low production yields. Success of such measurements requires both dedicated experimental techniques and strong theoretical support. Laser resonance chromatography (LRC) is a pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012801] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper performs ab initio electronic structure calculations for Ac+ to support laser resonance chromatography experiments.
motivation: Accurate spectroscopic data for heavy elements like actinium are needed to interpret experimental measurements, but are difficult to obtain due to short lifetimes and low production yields.
method: The authors use relativistic multi-configuration Dirac-Hartree-Fock and configuration interaction methods to compute energy levels and transition probabilities for Ac+.
result: They provide calculated energy levels and transition rates for low-lying states of Ac+, which can guide experimental searches.
conclusion: The theoretical predictions will aid in the identification of spectral lines in laser resonance chromatography experiments on Ac+.

title: High-precision Calculation Of Resonant Electronic Recombination And Resonant Transfer Excitation Cross Sections In Na-like ${\mathrm{Fe}}^{15+}$ Ions
authors: Wenliang He, Luyou Xie, Chengpeng Yang, Yulong Ma, And Chenzhong Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Wenliang He, Luyou Xie, Chengpeng Yang, Yulong Ma, and Chenzhong Dong

Large-scale level-by-level calculations have been systematically performed to obtain the [MATH]-shell resonant electronic recombination cross sections of [MATH] ions, using the relativistic configuration interaction method considering the complex electronic correlations, the Breit and QE…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012803] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates resonant electronic recombination and resonant transfer excitation cross sections for Na-like Fe15+ ions using relativistic configuration interaction.
motivation: Accurate cross sections are needed for modeling astrophysical and fusion plasmas, but previous calculations lacked precision due to complex electronic correlations.
method: Large-scale level-by-level calculations were performed using the relativistic configuration interaction method, including Breit and QED corrections.
result: High-precision cross sections were obtained for K-shell resonant electronic recombination of Fe15+ ions.
conclusion: The calculated cross sections improve atomic data for plasma diagnostics and modeling.

title: Ternary H-c-n Compounds At High Pressure Featuring $s{p}^{3}$-hybridized C-n Networks
authors: Bole Chen, Siyu Jin, Cheng Lu, And Andreas Hermann
abstract:
Author(s): Bole Chen, Siyu Jin, Cheng Lu, and Andreas Hermann

Hydrogen, carbon, and nitrogen are amongst the most important light elements in the composition of the solar system. They form the organic molecules and atmospheric components of many outer planets. Under the extreme conditions within planets, exploring the H-C-N chemical space is central to underst…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034109] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ternary H-C-N compounds under high pressure, focusing on crystal structures with sp3-hybridized C-N networks.
motivation: To understand the chemical behavior of light elements under extreme planetary conditions.
method: First-principles calculations using density functional theory to predict stable structures and properties.
result: Identified novel H-C-N compounds with sp3-hybridized carbon-nitrogen networks at high pressure.
conclusion: These compounds may exist in planetary interiors and have implications for planetary science.

title: Polar Magneto-optical Kerr Effect Of CoPt/AlN Multilayer Structures: Quantitative Determination Of The Off-diagonal Dielectric Permittivity Tensor Of CoPt
authors: Kejia Zhang, Kai Chen, Zihao Song, Haoyuan Deng, Yi Sun, Jundong Song, Takumi Sannomiya, Zhengjun Zhang, Takashi Harumoto, And Ji Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Kejia Zhang, Kai Chen, Zihao Song, Haoyuan Deng, Yi Sun, Jundong Song, Takumi Sannomiya, Zhengjun Zhang, Takashi Harumoto, and Ji Shi

CoPt alloy thin films as ferromagnetic metal materials have attracted widespread attention for magneto-optical (MO) applications due to their high perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and strong MO effect. However, quantitative determination of the off-diagonal dielectric permittivity tensor ${ɛ}…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantitatively determines the off-diagonal dielectric permittivity tensor of CoPt/AlN multilayer structures using polar magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements.
motivation: CoPt alloy thin films are promising for magneto-optical applications due to their high perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and strong MO effect, but quantitative determination of the off-diagonal dielectric permittivity tensor is needed for device design.
method: The authors measure polar magneto-optical Kerr effect spectra and fit them using a multilayer optical model to extract the off-diagonal permittivity tensor components of CoPt.
result: They obtain the complex off-diagonal permittivity tensor of CoPt as a function of wavelength, showing strong MO activity in the UV-visible range.
conclusion: The extracted tensor values enable accurate modeling and optimization of CoPt-based magneto-optical devices.

title: Anomalous Disappearance Of Dark Trions Due To Auger Recombination In Hole-doped ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Monolayers
authors: Junghwan Kim, Dinh van Tuan, Sébastien Roux, Tilly Guyot, Xavier Marie, Cedric Robert, And Hanan Dery
abstract:
Author(s): Junghwan Kim, Dinh Van Tuan, Sébastien Roux, Tilly Guyot, Xavier Marie, Cedric Robert, and Hanan Dery

In photoluminescence experiments of hole-doped [MATH] monolayer, a counterintuitive phenomenon is observed: the emission from the lower-energy dark positive trion ([MATH]) anomalously diminishes at high hole densities, while the signal from the higher-energy bright positive…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065406] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the anomalous disappearance of dark trion photoluminescence in hole-doped WSe2 monolayers due to Auger recombination.
motivation: To understand the counterintuitive observation that lower-energy dark trion emission diminishes at high hole densities while higher-energy bright trion emission persists.
method: Photoluminescence experiments on hole-doped WSe2 monolayers combined with theoretical modeling of Auger recombination processes.
result: The dark trion emission anomalously decreases at high hole densities due to efficient Auger recombination involving dark trions and free holes.
conclusion: Auger recombination is the dominant mechanism causing the disappearance of dark trions, which has implications for understanding exciton dynamics in 2D materials.

title: Strain Engineering Of Dielectric Properties And Phase Transitions In Orthorhombic $\mathrm{Hf}{\mathrm{O}}_{2}$
authors: Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, And Wei Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Mengyuan Yang, Shuai Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yongchang Li, Zhe Su, Yingtao Yang, Ruiling Gao, Zhaohe Gao, Chang Liu, Dongdong Li, Marcos José Leite Santos, Yin Wang, and Wei Ren

Hafnium dioxide ([MATH]), commonly known as hafnia, serves as a critical high-[MATH] gate dielectric material in complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) devices and is also widely utilized in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) capacitors. To gain better understanding of t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain engineering of dielectric properties and phase transitions in orthorhombic HfO2, a material science topic with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand and control the dielectric properties and phase transitions of hafnia for CMOS and DRAM applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to simulate strain effects on orthorhombic HfO2.
result: Strain can tune dielectric constants and induce phase transitions among different orthorhombic phases.
conclusion: Strain engineering is an effective way to modify dielectric properties of HfO2 for microelectronic applications.

title: Study Of The Boson Peak In Amorphous Ge-Sb-Te Using Machine Learning Potentials
authors: Pyungjin Park And Seung-Hoon Jhi
abstract:
Author(s): Pyungjin Park and Seung-Hoon Jhi

An excess of low-frequency vibrational states beyond the Debye prediction—known as the boson peak—is a universal feature of disordered materials, yet its microscopic origin and connection to atomic-scale structural disorder remain unresolved. Here we study the microscopic origin and real time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the boson peak in amorphous Ge-Sb-Te using machine learning potentials, focusing on vibrational anomalies in disordered materials.
motivation: The boson peak is a universal feature of disordered materials whose microscopic origin remains unresolved, and understanding it is important for materials science.
method: The authors use machine learning potentials to simulate atomic-scale structural disorder and analyze low-frequency vibrational states in amorphous Ge-Sb-Te.
result: The study identifies the microscopic origin of the boson peak and its real-time evolution in the disordered material.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the connection between atomic-scale disorder and vibrational anomalies, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superconductivity Of non-A15 Compounds In V-Sn Binary System
authors: Xin Li, Guo-Yong Shi, Rui-Tong Xiao, Zhi-Zhuo Liu, Hong Jiang, Yue-Hua Su, Huai-Jun Sun, Cai-Zhuang Wang, And Chao Zhang

By combining a genetic algorithm for crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations, both thermodynamically stable and metastable phases in the V-Sn binary system are systematically investigated. The experimentally synthesized A15-type [MATH] and ${…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates thermodynamically stable and metastable phases in the V-Sn binary system using crystal structure prediction and first-principles calculations, focusing on superconductivity of non-A15 compounds.
motivation: To explore new superconducting phases beyond the well-known A15 compounds in the V-Sn system.
method: Combined genetic algorithm for crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations to systematically search for stable and metastable phases.
result: Identified several thermodynamically stable and metastable phases, including non-A15 compounds with potential superconductivity.
conclusion: The V-Sn binary system hosts a variety of superconducting phases beyond A15, which may be of interest for materials science.

title: Interaction Of Solitons With Saturable Gain
authors: Akhilesh K. S. And Omri Gat
